input.command: entire brain setup --help 2>&1 | head -60
input.description: Show brain setup help

result.output:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (code index, sessions,
               repository context, docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO
               agent tokens. The brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. Background distillation has a
recurring cost, bounded by five gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends
(default no, and a run with no terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the code index, the repository context or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and
"entire brain overview" read, so "entire brain setup && entire brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale code index beside repository context
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints
the reason. setup exits non-zero when nothing usable exists: the brain
directory cannot be built, every component failed, the worktree is too dirty to
index, or the repository has no commits yet.

Re-running setup is safe: it detects the existing workspace membership and
daemon instead of duplicating them, resumes rather than restarts a backfill
that is still running, and keeps whatever --interval/--distill-every/--model/
--effort the previous run was given unless you pass the flag again.

Usage:
  entire-brain setup [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string             Agent for the background backfill: auto, none, codex, claude-code (default "auto")
      --agent-hooks              Merge the Claude Code PreToolUse entry even if a previous run declined it
      --backfill                 Start the background fact backfill even if a previous run declined it (SPENDS TOKENS)
      --backfill-budget int      Cap sessions the background backfill distills in one pass, newest first (0 = explicitly unlimited: the WHOLE corpus in one spend) (default 25)
      --daemon                   Install the background watcher even if a previous run declined it
      --distill-every duration   Minimum interval between the daemon's gated agent runs (default 24h0m0s)
      --effort string            Reasoning effort for the background backfill (default "low")
  -h, --help                     help for setup
      --interval duration        Daemon poll interval (default 5m0s)

An error saying the Keychain is not accessible or the network is not allowed means the sandbox blocked it, not that the user is logged out: ask to re-run it unsandboxed, and do not run `entire login`. A project trail spans repositories; each change is its branch in one repository. Project trails and changes are numbered separately: never pass

where a change is expected, or where a project trail is. Pass / to checkout, resume, finding, watch, approvals or approve; given to show, it shows the parent project trail. Users paste Entire trail URLs. Do not pass a URL to any command; map the path after the host to a selector: //-/trails/

/changes/ change / ///trails/ change / //-/trails/

project trail

Add --project / unless is origin's owner. To link a trail or change, use the url `entire trail show` prints. Scope: one project; --project is required, even inside a clone. --repo only filters within that project. --mine instead lists your trails across every project. Reports unique flagged source files, percentages, the inclusive 5% degradation threshold, language and diagnostic breakdowns, affected files and parser diagnostic locations. Documentation, configuration and data do not dilute the source denominator. Intentional skips are listed separately; stronger unsafe and unusable-graph safeguards still apply. 1	# Entire for VS Code
2	
3	Browse the [Entire](https://entire.com) checkpoints behind your commits, the agent sessions behind each checkpoint, and the trails of a repository on entire.com, in the editor where you read the code.
4	
5	![The Checkpoints and Sessions views in the sidebar, beside a checkpoint open in the detail panel with its files and transcript](images/checkpoint.png)
6	
7	## What You Get
8	
9	**Checkpoints view.** Lists each commit on the current branch that carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. One session produces a checkpoint for every commit made while it runs, so each row names the agent and says where its checkpoint sits in that session, such as 12 of 249. A commit expands only when there is something to tell apart: several checkpoints, as in a squash, or a checkpoint that holds several sessions. Checkpoints that no commit on the branch carries, such as imported ones, appear under Other Checkpoints. The list shows 50 commits at a time and loads the next 50 when you scroll to its end.
10	
11	**Sessions view.** Lists the sessions running now, then the rest by recency, each with its checkpoints under it. When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, the view reads the repository's sessions from Entire, as the Sessions page of entire.com lists them: every session on every branch, under the name Entire gave it, with Entire's count of its checkpoints. Expanding a session lists the checkpoints your clone knows at once, and adds the ones Entire lists for it, such as those on other branches. In any other repository, a session appears when Entire has local state for it or when a checkpoint references it, and it is named by the prompt that opened it. The view loads 50 sessions at a time in the same way.
12	
13	**Detail panel.** Click a commit, checkpoint, or session to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the commit, the files the session touched with a diff for each, and the transcript. Tool calls start collapsed, and expanding one shows its input and result. A checkpoint opens at its own part of the conversation, and Show Earlier Messages loads what came before. The panel says which checkpoint of the session it shows, and Previous and Next step through the session's other checkpoints. The selected row moves with the tab: the view you opened the tab from selects the row of the checkpoint the tab shows, and loads more of its list when that row is beyond the end.
14	
15	**Trails view.** Appears when the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme. It lists the trails that touch the repository, most recent activity first, 50 at a time. Each row shows the trail's number, its phase, and its branch in this repository, and marks the trail whose branch you have checked out.
16	
17	A trail is open or closed, and an open trail is in a phase: planning, building, or complete. The filter button in the view's title bar shows only the trails in one of those states: All, Open, Closed, Planning, Building, or Complete. The view starts on Open and names the filter in use beside its title.
18	
19	**Trail panel.** Click a trail to open it in an editor tab. The panel shows the trail's description and its branches, which Entire calls changes. For a change it shows whether the branch can merge, each merge gate with the reason for its result, and the CI runs on the head commit. Below that is the change's timeline of commits, reviews, and resolved findings. A commit that is in your clone and carries a checkpoint has an Open Checkpoint button, which opens the session behind the commit in the detail panel.
20	
21	The panel fills in as the Entire CLI answers. It draws the title and status from the Trails view at once, then the changes, then the timeline. A trail you opened earlier in the same window shows from that read at once, and the panel reads it again and redraws what has changed.
22	
23	![The Trails and Brain views in the sidebar, beside a trail open in the trail panel with its merge gates, CI runs, and timeline](images/trail.png)
24	
25	**Links to entire.com.** When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, each commit, session, and trail gets an Open on entire.com action.
26	
27	**Brain view.** The last section of the sidebar, shown when Entire is enabled in the repository and collapsed until you open it. It lists what the [entire-brain plugin](https://docs.entire.io/guides/brain/overview) reports about the repository's brain: whether it is built and when it was updated, the size of its code graph, its memories, conversations, and docs, whether it is up to date, whether background updates are running, and whether it is connected to a hosted brain. Anything that needs a look is marked, with the reason on hover. These details are text: only the section's buttons can be clicked.
28	
29	The View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in your browser. The page draws the code entities in the brain and the calls and imports between them. The same button is in the section's title bar, and the command palette has Entire: View Brain. While the page's server runs, the section says where and has a Stop button. Closing the window stops it too.
30	
31	## Requirements
32	
33	- [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) 0.12.0 or later. The extension reads checkpoints and sessions through it.
34	- Git.
35	- A local repository with Entire enabled (`entire enable`), opened as a trusted workspace.
36	- For the Brain view, the entire-brain plugin (`entire plugin install brain`) and a brain for the repository (`entire brain setup`).
37	- For the Trails view, an `entire://` origin and a login saved with `entire login`. Trails are stored on Entire, not in the clone, so the view lists them whether or not Entire is enabled there.
38	- For session names from Entire, the same origin and login. Without them, the Sessions view names each session by its opening prompt.
39	
40	The extension looks for `entire` on your `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `/usr/local/bin`, and then asks your login shell. Set `entire.cliPath` if the binary lives somewhere else.
41	
42	## Getting Started
43	
44	1. Install the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) and run `entire enable` in your repository.
45	2. Install Entire from the Extensions view in VS Code, Cursor, or another editor that installs from Open VSX.
46	3. Select the Entire icon in the activity bar.
47	
48	## Settings
49	
50	| Setting | Default | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| `entire.cliPath` | empty | Absolute path to the Entire CLI binary. |
53	| `entire.loadOnScroll` | `true` | Load the next 50 rows of a list when you scroll to its end. When off, click Load More. |
54	| `entire.trails.enabled` | `true` | Show the Trails view and read trails from Entire. When off, the view is hidden and the extension runs no `entire trail` command. |
55	| `entire.webBaseUrl` | empty | Base URL for links to the Entire web app. When empty, the extension uses `ENTIRE_WEB_BASE_URL` if it is set, and `https://entire.com` otherwise. |
56	
57	## What the Extension Runs
58	
59	The extension is a read-only explorer. It does not create, edit, or delete checkpoints, and it does not run `entire enable` for you. It runs these commands in your repository:
60	
61	| Command | When |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| `git log`, `git cat-file`, `git for-each-ref`, `git diff-tree` | To list commits, read stored transcripts, and build diffs. |
64	| `entire status --json` | On load and on each automatic refresh. |
65	| `entire checkpoint explain --json` | In the background, to add each checkpoint's agent and sessions to the views. |
66	| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>` | When you expand or open a checkpoint. |
67	| `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --short` | When you open a checkpoint that no commit in the history read so far carries, to learn who its author is. Once for each such checkpoint. |
68	| `entire session list --json` | When the Sessions view is first shown, and when you click Refresh. |
69	| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions?scope=all&limit=50` | When the Sessions view is first shown, when its list loads the next page, and when you click Refresh. Only for an `entire://` origin. |
70	| `entire api --to cell /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/sessions/<session>/transcript` | When you expand or open a session for which Entire counts more checkpoints than your clone knows. Once for each such session, until you click Refresh. |
71	| `entire trail list --json` | When the Trails view is first shown, when you change the filter to another status, when the list loads its next page, and when you click Refresh. |
72	| `entire trail show <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, and the first time you open or copy a trail's link from its row. |
73	| `entire trail timeline <trail> --json` | When you open or refresh a trail, switch to another of its changes, or load more of its timeline. Opening a trail runs it once or twice: the panel asks for the trail's timeline while it reads the trail, and asks again for one change by name when the trail has several changes or a change whose branch is gone. |
74	| `entire brain status --json` | When the Brain view is first opened, when you click Refresh after that, and when you open the brain graph. |
75	| `entire brain viz --no-open --port 0` | When you open the brain graph and its server is not running for the repository. The plugin serves the page on 127.0.0.1 until you stop it or close the window. |
76	
77	Two of these have effects inside the Entire CLI. `entire checkpoint explain` fetches checkpoint data from your checkpoint remote when it is missing from the local clone. `entire session list` removes session state that has been idle for more than seven days, which is why the extension keeps it out of automatic refresh.
78	
79	The extension sends no network requests of its own. The three trail commands and the two `entire api` calls make the Entire CLI read Entire over the network with your saved login. The extension runs them only for a repository whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme, and not before the view that needs them is on screen. Turn off the `entire.trails.enabled` setting to hide the Trails view and stop the extension from running the trail commands. It runs none of the trail commands that write, such as `entire trail approve` or `entire trail merge`.
80	
81	`entire api` is the CLI's authenticated request to Entire's API. The extension gives it a path and nothing else, which makes it a GET: it passes no method, field, or body. The CLI calls these endpoints internal and says their shape can change without notice. When a read fails, or returns something the extension does not recognize, the Sessions view shows what your clone knows, with each session named by its opening prompt.
82	
83	The brain graph is served on your machine by the entire-brain plugin, on the loopback address. The plugin describes the page as read-only, with no outbound network. The extension opens only that local address.
84	
85	Open Raw Transcript has the Entire CLI write the transcript to a file in a private temporary directory, opens it read-only, and removes it when the window closes. A raw transcript can run to hundreds of megabytes, so it goes to a file instead of through memory.
86	
87	## Limits
88	
89	- The Checkpoints view follows the history of `HEAD`. Other branches appear after you check them out.
90	- Loading on scroll pauses when it reads 20,000 commits without finding a checkpoint. Click Load More Checkpoints to read further back.
91	- A commit can name a checkpoint whose session data was never uploaded. The commit carries the checkpoint's ID, and the Entire CLI uploads the data separately. Opening one shows the commit and its diff with a note in place of the transcript, and its row then reads "no session data".
92	- A session with no checkpoint yet shows its facts and its raw transcript, with no chat view.
93	- The selected row follows a tab only in the view the tab was opened from, and only while that view is on screen. The other view keeps its own selection. A tab opened from a trail is followed by the Checkpoints view. A tab opened on a session's own row has no Previous and Next, so its selection stays on the session.
94	- Session names come from Entire only for an `entire://` origin and a saved login. The view reads them when it is first shown and when you click Refresh, and it does not follow changes on Entire in between. A session that Entire has not listed yet, such as one that is still running, is named as in any other repository until then.
95	- Without Entire's list, a session's name is read from the start of the normalized transcript that its checkpoints store. A session with no checkpoint shows its latest prompt in its place. A session whose checkpoints store no normalized transcript, as some Codex sessions do not, shows the message of its newest checkpoint until you open it, and its opening prompt after that.
96	- Entire's count of a session's checkpoints can be higher than the number its page on entire.com lists. In testing, a session counted at 36 listed 29. A session's row shows the count until you expand it, and the number of checkpoints listed after that.
97	- Entire sends a session's checkpoints with its transcript. In testing that took two to eight seconds, so the checkpoints your clone knows show first and the rest are added when they arrive.
98	- Entire can list a checkpoint whose session data the Entire CLI cannot find in your clone or on the checkpoint remote. Opening one shows a note in place of the transcript, and Open on entire.com shows the session there.
99	- A transcript does not record who sent its prompts. The panel names the author of the commit that carries the checkpoint, as the Entire CLI does. For a checkpoint with no commit in the history read so far, it names the author the CLI reports, which arrives a moment after the transcript. A prompt reads "User" when neither is known.
100	- The chat view reads the normalized transcript that Entire stores in each checkpoint. A session without one falls back to the Entire CLI's text view, which omits tool inputs and results and covers the latest session of a checkpoint.
101	- The agent on a commit row, a checkpoint's place in its session, and the checkpointed sessions in the Sessions view come from the Entire CLI, which reports the newest 500 commits of the current branch. Older commits show commit details until you open them. A plus sign, as in 210+, marks a session at the old end of that list, which may have earlier checkpoints.
102	- Links to entire.com need an `entire://` origin. A repository connected to Entire through the GitHub App with a `github.com` origin gets no links and no Trails view.
103	- The Trails view lists the trails that touch the repository of the `origin` remote. It reads them when it is first shown and when you click Refresh, and it does not follow changes on Entire in between.
104	- The Entire CLI lists trails by status and not by phase. For the Planning, Building, and Complete filters, the extension reads the open trails and keeps the ones in that phase, at most four pages of 50 for each load. It cannot know how many trails in the phase are left, so the Load More row says how many trails it has read, as in 10 shown · 200 of 1,240 read.
105	- The Trails view and the trail panel are read-only. Change a trail's status, comment on it, review it, approve it, and merge it on entire.com or with the Entire CLI.
106	- In testing, the Entire CLI took about one second to read a trail and two to three seconds to read a timeline, whatever the page size. The trail panel reads both at once and draws each when it arrives. The timeline of a change whose branch is gone, such as a merged branch that was deleted, takes about a second longer, because the CLI finds that change only by a number that the trail has to supply first.
107	- The brain graph opens in your browser, not in an editor tab. The plugin's page forbids other pages from embedding it.
108	- The Brain view reads the brain when you first open it and when you click Refresh. It does not follow the brain's changes in between.
109	- The brain graph's server keeps its port until you run Entire: Stop Brain Graph or close the window. It reads the checked-out branch when it starts, so the extension starts it again when you open the graph on another branch.
110	- The extension does not install the entire-brain plugin, build a brain, or refresh one. When either is missing, it shows the command to run.
111	- The trail panel shows the timeline of one change at a time. A commit in it opens its checkpoint only when the commit is in your clone, so fetch the trail's branch to open the rest. For a change in another repository of the project, the panel lists the commits and opens none of them.
112	
113	## Feedback
114	
115	Report a problem or ask for a feature in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/entireio/entire-vscode/issues). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers building and testing the extension. Report a security vulnerability the way [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says, and not in an issue.
116

118	
119	[MIT](LICENSE). [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) lists the code from other projects that ships inside the extension.
120

1	# Contributing
2	
3	## Development
4	
5	Node 22.18 or later is required.
6	
7	```sh
8	npm install
9	npm run build                      # bundle the extension and the panel into dist/
10	npm run check                      # lint, type-check, and unit tests
11	npm run test:host                  # run the extension in a VS Code instance against a fixture repository
12	npm run smoke -- /path/to/repo     # print what the extension would show for a real repository
13	npm run notices                    # rewrite THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md after a bundled dependency changes
14	```
15	
16	Press F5 in VS Code to start an Extension Development Host with the extension loaded.
17	
18	The extension-host tests open real editor windows, one per launch, and close them when they finish. The windows start with Chromium's background throttling turned off, because they usually sit behind your other windows and the editor slows down there.
19	
20	The extension-host tests run in VS Code by default. To run them in another editor built on VS Code, point `ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR` at its executable. Each launch uses a profile of its own, so the editor's real settings and extensions are left alone.
21	
22	```sh
23	ENTIRE_TEST_EDITOR=/Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/MacOS/Cursor npm run test:host
24	npx vscode-test --code-version 1.95.0    # the oldest VS Code the manifest allows
25	```
26	
27	## Layout
28	
29	| Path | Contents |
30	| --- | --- |
31	| `src/core` | Git and Entire CLI logic. It does not import `vscode`, so it runs under plain Node in tests. |
32	| `src/ext` | Tree views, commands, file watchers, and the panel hosts. |
33	| `src/webview` | The UI of the detail panel and the trail panel, bundled separately for the browser. One bundle serves both, and the host says which page to draw. |
34	| `src/shared` | Message types that the host and the panels both use. |
35	| `test/unit`, `test/webview` | `vitest` tests. Webview tests run on `happy-dom`, except the Markdown sanitizer tests and the trail panel tests, which need `jsdom` because DOMPurify does not work on `happy-dom`. |
36	| `test/integration` | Tests that run inside a VS Code extension host. |
37	| `test/fake-entire` | A stand-in for the Entire CLI that replays canned output. |
38	
39	Ten things are easy to break without noticing:
40	
41	- Automatic refresh calls `entire status --json` and git only. `entire session list` prunes old session state, so it runs when the Sessions view is first shown and on a manual refresh. An extension-host test asserts this.
42	- A list loads its next page when its Load More row scrolls into view. Tree views report nothing about scrolling, so `src/ext/views/scrollLoader.ts` relies on the editor asking for a row's file decoration when it draws the row. The row's `resourceUri` is what makes that work, and the extension-host tests in `test/integration/scroll.test.cjs` fail if an editor stops asking that way.
43	- The selected row follows the detail tab (`src/ext/views/selectionSync.ts`). A click selects a row, but Previous and Next move the tab without a click, and `TreeView.reveal` is the only way to move a selection. `reveal` takes a row object and looks for it among the ones the editor was given. An equal row that is another object is not found, and VS Code 1.95 refuses it as a duplicate. So the Checkpoints and Sessions trees hand out one object for each row ID and update it in place (`src/ext/views/rowRegistry.ts`). Do not return a freshly built row from `getChildren` past the registry, and do not keep a row object to compare its old fields with later ones. `reveal` also opens the sidebar on a view that is hidden, so a view that is not visible is left alone. The tests in `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` run against a real tree view, and are worth running on the oldest supported editor after a change here.
44	- A raw transcript goes from the CLI straight to a temporary file (`src/ext/transcriptFiles.ts`), not into memory. One long session's transcript measured 178 MB. Open such files with the `vscode.open` command: the extension host refuses to load documents over 50 MB.
45	- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` is the only module that knows how checkpoints are stored in git. It exists to read the normalized transcript, which no CLI command outputs, and every reader in it falls back to the CLI on a surprise. The transcript is read whole to show it, and its first lines are read to name a session by its opening prompt. Most transcripts hold the session from its start, so each checkpoint of a session gives the same opening prompt. A transcript with no start line holds only its checkpoint's part, and its first prompt is not taken for the session's unless the checkpoint is the session's first.
46	- Trails and Entire's session list are the two features that reach the network. Trails go through `entire trail list`, `show`, and `timeline`. Those three only read. The other trail commands write, and the extension runs none of them. Nothing calls the three until the Trails view is on screen, which `test/integration/states.test.cjs` asserts, and nothing calls them while the `entire.trails.enabled` setting is off, which `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` asserts. A trail's web address comes from `entire trail show`, because the CLI asks callers not to build one. The CLI lists trails by status only, so `src/core/trails.ts` matches a phase filter against the trails read so far and limits how many pages one load may read.
47	- The Sessions view takes its names from Entire's API, through `entire api --to cell` (`src/core/remoteSessions.ts`, and `remoteSessions` and `remoteSessionCheckpoints` in `src/core/entireCli.ts`). The calls pass a path and no other flag, so the CLI sends a GET, and a test in `test/unit/remoteSessionsCli.test.ts` fails if a method, field, or body flag appears. The CLI calls these endpoints internal, so the readers take only the fields they know and every failure falls back to what the clone knows: the session list from the CLI and git, with names from stored transcripts. The API answers a refusal as JSON on stdout with a non-zero exit, which is why these calls do not use `jsonResult`. Nothing reads the list until the Sessions view is on screen, and automatic refresh never reads it, which `test/integration/extension.test.cjs` and `test/integration/states.test.cjs` assert. A session's checkpoints come with its whole transcript, so that call runs only for a session whose count on Entire exceeds what the clone knows, once, and the rows the clone knows are drawn without waiting for it.
48	- The trail panel reads a trail and its timeline side by side, because each call takes seconds (`src/ext/panel/trailPanelController.ts`). Until the trail is read, the timeline call can name only the trail, and the CLI then picks the change without saying which one it read. The panel uses that answer only when the trail has one change, and asks for the change by name otherwise. The CLI picks by branch, so it refuses a change whose branch is gone, and the panel asks for such a change by name without waiting for the refusal. `test/integration/trails.test.cjs` has a trail for each case. What the panel keeps in `src/core/trailMemory.ts` is a head start: it reads a trail again each time it draws one from there.
49	- The brain graph is a server that the extension starts and has to stop (`src/ext/brainService.ts`, `src/core/serverProcess.ts`). `entire brain viz` runs until it is stopped, as a child of the Entire CLI, so the extension stops the whole process group, and it stops every server when the window closes. The plugin's page forbids framing, which is why it opens in the browser and not in a panel. The address the extension opens is rebuilt from the port in the plugin's ready line (`parseVizUrl` in `src/core/brain.ts`) and is never that line's text. Nothing runs a brain command until the Brain view, which starts collapsed, is opened or View Brain is used. `test/integration/states.test.cjs` asserts that in windows whose sidebar stays closed. That file's fake server prints an address and serves nothing, so run the command against a real brain after a change here.
50	- The Brain view is a page and not a tree (`src/core/brainPage.ts`, `src/ext/views/brainView.ts`). Every row of a tree view looks clickable, and the brain's details are text with nothing to click. The page has no script. Its buttons are links to commands, and the view lets the editor run only the commands in `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`. A row that does nothing does not belong in a tree view: put it on a page, or leave it out.
51	
52	## Screenshots
53	
54	The two pictures in `images/` are of the extension in VS Code, on a demo repository with made-up commits, sessions, and trails. The fake Entire CLI in `test/fake-entire` supplies the data, as it does for the extension-host tests. Retake them when a view changes, and take them from made-up data: a screenshot of a real repository publishes its session names, prompts, and transcripts.
55	
56	The README links to them by relative path. `vsce` rewrites those links to this repository on GitHub when it packages the extension, so the pictures are not in the VSIX, and they show on the Marketplace only while the repository is public.
57	
58	## Releasing
59	
60	A release is a tag. Pushing `v<version>` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds the VSIX once and publishes that one file to the Visual Studio Marketplace, to Open VSX, and to a GitHub release for the tag. The release takes its notes from the version's entry in `CHANGELOG.md`, and its VSIX is the file to install by hand with Extensions: Install from VSIX.
61	
62	1. Update `version` in `package.json` and add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.
63	2. Run `npm run check`, `npm run test:host`, and `npm run package`. The last command writes `entire-<version>.vsix`.
64	3. Install that file with `code --install-extension entire-<version>.vsix` and open a repository that has checkpoints.
65	4. Commit, then tag and push the tag: `git tag v<version>` and `git push origin v<version>`.
66	
67	### One-Time Setup
68	
69	**Visual Studio Marketplace.** The workflow signs in with [GitHub Trusted Publishing](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension), so the repository stores no Marketplace token. The personal access tokens that `vsce` used before are retired on December 1, 2026.
70	
71	1. Create the publisher `entire` at [marketplace.visualstudio.com/manage](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/manage). Its ID has to match `publisher` in `package.json`, and it cannot be changed later.
72	2. Open the publisher, select Trusted Publishing, and create a policy with repository owner `entireio`, repository `entire-vscode`, workflow `release.yml`, and environment `marketplace`.
73	
74	**Open VSX.** The steps are in the [Open VSX publishing guide](https://github.com/eclipse/openvsx/wiki/Publishing-Extensions).
75	
76	1. Create an Eclipse account, sign in to open-vsx.org with GitHub, and accept the Publisher Agreement in the profile settings.
77	2. Generate an access token under Settings, Access Tokens, and create the namespace with `npx ovsx create-namespace entire -p <token>`.
78	3. Save the token as the secret `OVSX_PAT` in the repository's `open-vsx` environment.
79	
80	The two publish jobs run in the `marketplace` and `open-vsx` environments. Add required reviewers to them in the repository settings if a release should wait for an approval.
81

content.text: While the explorations run, there are three design choices that depend on what you want, so I'll ask now.

questions.question: The README promises the extension is read-only and never runs `entire enable` or installs/builds the brain for you. For the new Setup flow, how should the setup commands (install CLI, login, enable, plugin installs, graph setup, brain setup, brain connect) run?

options.label: Integrated terminal (Recommended)
options.description: Each step's button opens a VS Code terminal and runs the command there, so interactive prompts (agent picker, browser login, Brain token-spend question) work and the user sees everything. The extension re-checks status when the command ends.

options.label: Background, no terminal
options.description: The extension runs each step itself with non-interactive flags (--yes, --agent ...), shows progress notifications, and only falls back to a terminal for login. Faster, but it makes choices (agents, telemetry, backfill) on the user's behalf.

options.label: Copy commands only
options.description: Keep the read-only promise: the Setup flow shows each step's status and a Copy button for its command; the user runs it themselves.

questions.question: Where should the Setup flow live?

options.label: Sidebar Setup page (Recommended)
options.description: A 'Setup' webview section in the Entire sidebar, shown when anything is missing: a live checklist (CLI, Login, Enable, Graph, Brain, Brain Connect), each row with its state and a button. Replaces today's 'not enabled / CLI missing' welcome text.

options.label: VS Code walkthrough
options.description: A native Get Started walkthrough (contributes.walkthroughs) with one step per item; steps tick off via context keys. Opens from a sidebar link and on first activation. Less live status detail.

options.label: Both
options.description: Sidebar checklist for status and actions, plus a walkthrough that explains each step for first-time users.

options.label: Quick Pick + view buttons (Recommended)
options.description: 'Entire: Search' opens a Quick Pick that queries as you type: Entire's hosted search (`entire search --json`) for checkpoints, commits and sessions, and the trail list filtered by title/number/body. A search icon in each view's title bar opens it scoped to that view. Picking a hit opens the existing detail or trail panel. Falls back to the loaded local lists when not logged in.

options.label: Filter the tree views
options.description: A search icon in each view's title bar filters that view's rows in place (with a Clear Filter button), like the Trails status filter today. Hosted search fills in hits the clone has not loaded.

options.label: Dedicated Search view
options.description: A new 'Search' section in the sidebar with an input box and grouped results (Checkpoints, Sessions, Trails) that stay on screen while you open them.

Usage:
  entire graph doctor [--json] [--assert "<command line>"]

Reports the resolved repo, the Entire environment variables, plugin-data-dir writability, and confirms no_egress=true (no remote fetches, hosted APIs, telemetry, or grammar downloads).

--assert is the preflight: it parses a command line against this binary and exits non-zero if this binary would reject it, WITHOUT running anything — no repo read, no index build, no writes. Run it once before a batch or a benchmark cell so a flag set built for a different build fails at startup instead of failing the first call of every session and leaving an agent to explore by hand. Repeatable. It runs each command's real parser, so a command that requires a flag will say so; assert the command line you actually intend to run.

Flags:
  --json               Emit the report as JSON
  --assert <cmdline>   Verify this binary accepts a command line, without running it (repeatable)

Examples:
  entire graph doctor --json
  entire graph doctor --assert "query --profile full --top-k 10 --format text"

# Search and Entire Setup for the VS Code Extension

## Context

The extension lists checkpoints, sessions, and trails, but you cannot search them: the only way to find one is to scroll. Also, when Entire is missing in a repository, the views show a line of text and a Copy Command button for each missing piece. CLI install, login, enable, Graph, Brain, and Brain connect are each handled differently, and Graph and Brain connect aren't handled at all.

This change adds two things:

1. **Search.** An `Entire: Search` Quick Pick that searches as you type. Each view gets a search button that opens it limited to that view.
2. **Entire Setup.** A Setup page in the sidebar: a live checklist of the CLI, Login, Enable, Graph, Brain, and Brain Connect steps. Each step's button runs its command in an integrated terminal, and the page checks the step again when the command ends.

Choices you made (asked during planning): commands run in an integrated terminal, setup lives on a sidebar Setup page, and search is a Quick Pick plus a button on each view.

This reverses the README's promise that the extension "does not run `entire enable` for you" and does not install or build the brain. The extension still runs setup commands only in a visible terminal, and only when you click a step, so the README and CONTRIBUTING change with it.

## What the CLI Gives Us (Checked Against CLI 0.13.4, graph v0.6.0, brain v0.5.1)

- `entire search --json --limit N -- <query>` searches checkpoints and sessions on Entire, about 2 seconds per query.
  - It needs a login, and it searches the current repository by default.
  - `--` is accepted before a query, which keeps a query that starts with `-` from being read as a flag.
  - Results arrive as `{results:[{type, data, searchMeta}], total, page, total_pages, counts}`. The types are `commit`, `session`, `checkpoint`, `pr`, and `repo`.
  - **Commit hits** carry `commitSha`, `commitSubject`, `commitMessage` (which holds the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer), `branch`, `author`, and `createdAt`.
  - **Session hits** carry `sessionId`, `matchedCheckpointId`, `displayName`, `prompt`, `agent`, `branch`, `createdAt`, and `searchMeta.snippet`.
  - **Checkpoint hits** never appeared in testing (`counts.checkpoints` was 0), so they are read defensively.
- Trails have no search command, so trails are matched on the client. Searching trails reads `entire trail list --json` with no status filter.
- `entire auth status --json` returns `{logged_in, user, ...}` in about 0.9 seconds.
- `entire graph version --json` exits 0 when the plugin is installed (0.1 seconds). Without the plugin, the CLI prints its usage and an `unknown command` error.
- `entire graph setup` writes `.entire/agent-guide.md` and adds a managed `<!-- entire-agent:begin -->` block to `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- `entire brain status --json` reports `brain.manifest_state`, plus `hosted.state` and `hosted.synced`. The extension already parses these in `readBrainStatus` (`src/core/brain.ts:70`).
- `entire brain connect` resolves the hosted repository through `entire repo view` and needs a login.
- Plugin index names are `graph` and `brain`: `entire plugin install graph|brain`.
- The install commands come from docs.entire.com/installation:
  - **macOS:** `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`, or the install script.
  - **Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash`.
  - **Windows:** `irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex`.

## Part 1: Search

### Core (`src/core/search.ts`, new; no `vscode` import)

- `SearchHit` is a union:
  - `{kind:'commit', sha, subject, checkpointIds, branch?, author?, createdAt?, score}`. The checkpoint IDs come from parsing the trailer with the existing trailer reader in `src/core/trailers.ts`.
  - `{kind:'session', sessionId, checkpointId?, name, prompt?, agent?, branch?, createdAt?, snippet?, score}`
  - `{kind:'checkpoint', checkpointId, ...}`
- `readSearchPage(value): SearchPage | undefined` follows the hand-written reader style of `schemas.ts`. It keeps only the fields it knows, skips `pr` and `repo` hits and anything malformed, and validates IDs with `isCheckpointId` and the `SESSION_ID` pattern.
- `isSearchQuery(text)` accepts 1–500 characters with no control characters.
- `matchesLocal(query, fields)` matches case-insensitively. Every word of the query has to appear in some field. Inline filters such as `author:` and `date:` are left out of local matching, except that `branch:x` filters on the branch field.
- `trailMatches(query, trail)` matches `#123` or `123` against the trail number, and words against the title, body, phase, and branch names.

### CLI (`src/core/entireCli.ts`)

- Add `search(cwd, query, limit, signal)`. It runs `['search', '--json', '--limit', String(limit), '--', query]` with a 30-second timeout and `TRAIL_FAILURES`-style wording (`remote: true`), so a missing login is classified as `notLoggedIn` and a repository Entire doesn't know as `noAccess`. It rejects a query that fails `isSearchQuery` before anything runs.

### Quick Pick (`src/ext/searchPicker.ts`, new)

- `entire.search` takes an optional scope (`'checkpoints' | 'sessions' | 'trails'`) and builds a `createQuickPick`, following the pattern of `pickTrailFilter` in `src/ext/commands.ts:96`.
- **Empty query.** The picker lists recent local items: the newest sessions and checkpoint commits.
- **On `onDidChangeValue`, local results come first and draw at once.** They come from data already loaded:
  - commits in `repo.index` (subject, SHA, checkpoint IDs)
  - `manager.sessions(repo)` (name, opening prompt, last prompt, ID, branch, agent)
  - `repo.trails`
- **Entire's search runs after that,** for the checkpoint and session scopes, debounced by 300 ms. It shows `busy` while it runs and aborts the previous query through an `AbortController`. It runs only when the query is at least 2 characters and `entire.search.hosted` is on.
- **Trails.** When the scope includes trails and `entire.trails.enabled` is on, each repository with `entireRepo` reads its trails once per picker. The read uses `status 'all'` and `readTrailPages` from `src/core/trails.ts`, at most 4 pages, and matches with `trailMatches`.
- **Merging.** Hits are grouped under separators: Checkpoints, Sessions, Trails. They are deduplicated by checkpoint ID, session ID, and SHA, with Entire's ranked hits first, then the remaining local matches. Every item has `alwaysShow: true`, because filtering is ours and not the Quick Pick's.
- **Item layout.**
  - Label: a codicon and the title.
  - Description: branch · agent · relative time, using `relativeTime` from `src/core/format.ts`.
  - Detail: the snippet, on one line, at most 120 characters.
- **Item buttons.** Open in New Tab, and Open on entire.com when the repository has `entireRepo`. They reuse the methods of `Actions` in `src/ext/actions.ts`.
- **Hint items.**
  - When Entire's search fails with `notLoggedIn`, an item reads "Log in to Entire to search sessions on Entire". It runs the Setup login step.
  - For `noAccess`, it reads "Entire does not know this repository".
  - For any other failure, it reads "Search on Entire failed" and opens the log.
- **On accept:**
  - **Commit or checkpoint with a checkpoint ID:** `panels.open({repoRoot, mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId, commitSha}, {newTab})`. The detail panel loads through `manager.detail`, which fetches from the checkpoint remote when the checkpoint is missing locally.
  - **Commit without a checkpoint:** `actions.showCommitDiff` when the commit is in the clone. Otherwise it opens on the web.
  - **Session the merged list knows:** `{mode:'session', sessionId}`. A session it doesn't know opens with `{mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId: matchedCheckpointId, sessionId}`, because session mode shows "no record" for sessions missing from `manager.sessions()` (`panelController.ts:399`). With no checkpoint either, it opens on the web.
  - **Trail:** `panels.openTrail({repoRoot, mode:'trail', trail: number, id})`.
- **Multi-root.** Searches run per repository. A repository's name goes in the description when more than one is open.

### Manifest

- Add the command `entire.search`, titled "Search" with the `$(search)` icon. In the command palette it shows when `entire.viewState == 'ready' || entire.hasTrails`.
- Add `view/title` entries at `navigation@0` on `entire.checkpoints`, `entire.sessions`, and `entire.trails`. Each passes its scope through a small wrapper command (`entire.searchCheckpoints`, and so on), hidden from the palette, because view/title menus can't pass arguments.
- Add the setting `entire.search.hosted`, default `true`. It controls whether search also asks Entire's search service. This matches the opt-out precedent of `entire.trails.enabled`.

## Part 2: Entire Setup

### Steps and How Each Is Detected

| Step | Done when | Command run in the terminal | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | `viewState` is past `cliMissing` and `cliTooOld` (existing `locateCli` and `version`) | A Quick Pick of install methods for this platform, each showing its exact command, plus Open Installation Docs. If the CLI is too old, the upgrade command for the way it was installed: Homebrew when the binary is under a Homebrew prefix, otherwise the script. | none |
| Login | `entire auth status --json` → `logged_in` | `entire login` | CLI |
| Enable | `repo.enabled` (existing `entire status --json`) | `entire enable` (interactive agent picker) | CLI |
| Graph | The plugin answers `entire graph version --json`, **and** `.entire/agent-guide.md` exists and mentions `entire graph` | `entire plugin install graph`, then `entire graph setup` (two buttons, one for each state) | CLI |
| Brain | `brainStatus` is not `pluginMissing`, and `manifest_state !== 'absent'` | `entire plugin install brain`, then `entire brain setup` | CLI |
| Brain Connect | Shown only for an `entire://` origin (`repo.entireRepo`), which is how the rest of the extension defines a hosted repository. Done when `hosted.state === 'connected'`. | `entire brain connect` | Login, Brain built |

- CLI and Enable are required, because the views need them. Login is recommended, because search, trails, session names, and Connect need it. Graph, Brain, and Connect are optional.
- Login and CLI apply to the whole machine. The other steps are listed per repository.

### Core (no `vscode` import)

- **`src/core/setup.ts`, new.**
  - `SetupStepId`.
  - `SetupFacts`: the CLI state, login, and for each repository enabled, graph plugin and guide, brain state, hosted, and connected.
  - `setupSteps(facts) → SetupStepView[]`, where each step has a state (`done | needed | optional | blocked | running | unknown`), a reason, and its actions.
  - `setupCommandLine(stepAction, cliPath, platform)`. It uses bare `entire` when the CLI was found on `PATH`. Otherwise it uses the quoted located path: single quotes on POSIX, `& '…'` on Windows. Only constant arguments are added after it.
  - `installOptions(platform, hasBrew)`.
- **`src/core/pageKit.ts`, new.** Moves `escapeHtml`, `commandHref`, `button`, and the base `STYLES` out of `src/core/brainPage.ts`, so the Setup page and the Brain page share them. `brainPage.ts` re-exports `escapeHtml` so existing imports keep working.
- **`src/core/setupPage.ts`, new.** `setupPageHtml(model, nonce)` and `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`. The page has no script, the same CSP as the Brain page, every piece of text escaped, and buttons that are command links with `[root, stepId]` arguments. Each row shows a status glyph and label (✓ Done, Needed, Optional, Running in terminal…, Needs …), the step's title, a sentence on what it gives you, and its button. The footer has Check Again and Hide Setup.
- **`src/core/schemas.ts`.** Add `readAuthStatus` (`logged_in`, `user`).
- **`src/core/entireCli.ts`.**
  - Add `authStatus(cwd)`: `auth status --json`, 15-second timeout, `dedupe`.
  - Add `graphVersion(cwd)`: `graph version --json`, 5 seconds. An `unknown command "graph` error maps to `pluginMissing`, by generalizing `isPluginMissing` in `src/core/brain.ts:240` to take the plugin name.

### Extension

- **`src/ext/setupTerminal.ts`, new.**
  - `run(root, label, commandLine): Promise<{exitCode?: number}>`. It reuses one terminal per repository root, named "Entire Setup" (with the repository name in multi-root windows), created with `cwd: root`, and calls `show()`.
  - If shell integration activates within 5 seconds (`terminal.shellIntegration` or `onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration`; stable since VS Code 1.93, and the engine floor is 1.95), it calls `shellIntegration.executeCommand(commandLine)` and resolves on `window.onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` for that execution, with its exit code.
  - Otherwise it calls `sendText(commandLine)` and resolves at once with no exit code. The page then says "Running in terminal. Click Check Again when it finishes." The setup service also checks again when the terminal closes and when the window regains focus.
- **`src/ext/setupService.ts`, new.**
  - Holds `SetupFacts` and the running step of each repository, and fires `onDidChange`.
  - `refresh()` reads the login, the Graph plugin, the guide file, and brain status for each repository, all in parallel. It runs only while the Setup view is visible, which keeps the CONTRIBUTING rule that nothing reads the network or runs a brain command while the sidebar is closed.
  - `runStep(root, stepId)` builds the command line, marks the step running, awaits the terminal, then refreshes. After CLI and Enable it also runs `manager.reload({manual:false})`, and after Brain steps it runs `brain.refresh()`.
  - Sets the context key `entire.showSetup` to `viewState ∈ {cliMissing, cliTooOld, notEnabled}`, or to whether you asked for setup this session (`entire.openSetup`), until Hide Setup.
- **`src/ext/views/setupView.ts`, new.** A `WebviewViewProvider` modeled on `BrainView` (`src/ext/views/brainView.ts`): `enableScripts: false`, `enableCommandUris: SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`, and a redraw only when the HTML changes. It calls `setup.refresh()` on the first resolve and each time it becomes visible.
- **`src/ext/brainService.ts`.** Expose a read that the setup service can trigger, which reuses the cached `BrainInfo`, so the Brain view and the Setup page share one `brain status` read.
- **`src/ext/repoManager.ts`.** Keep the located CLI path and its source (`cliPath`, `cliSource`) even when the version is too old, because the upgrade step and the command lines need them.
- **`src/ext/commands.ts`.**
  - Add `entire.openSetup` (sets the flag, then runs `entire.setup.focus`), `entire.runSetupStep(root, stepId)`, `entire.checkSetup`, and `entire.hideSetup`.
  - `entire.installCli` opens the install Quick Pick, which can also open the docs.
  - Keep the copy commands registered and hidden, so existing tests and keybindings don't break.
- **`src/core/brainPage.ts`.** The `pluginMissing` and `noBrain` notices get a primary "Run in Terminal" button (`entire.runSetupStep`) and keep Copy Command as a secondary button. Add the new command to `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- **`src/extension.ts`.** Construct the setup service, terminal runner, setup view, and search picker. Register the `entire.setup` view provider. Extend `EntireTestApi` with `setup` (facts and the last page HTML) and `search(query, scope)`, which returns the built items, and `acceptSearch(item)`, so the host tests can drive search without UI automation.

### Manifest

- Add a webview view `entire.setup`, named "Setup", first in the `entire` container, with `when: entire.showSetup`.
- Change the `viewsWelcome` entries for `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, and `notEnabled` on Checkpoints and Sessions to one sentence and `[Set Up Entire](command:entire.openSetup)`. The Retry link stays.
- Add the commands `entire.openSetup` ("Set Up Entire", in the palette), `entire.runSetupStep`, `entire.checkSetup`, and `entire.hideSetup` (the last three hidden from the palette). Add an overflow menu item "Set Up Entire…" on the Checkpoints view title.

## Docs

- **README.md:**
  - Add a "Search" section.
  - Add a "Setup" section.
  - Update Getting Started to: open the Entire view and follow Setup.
  - Add rows to the "What the Extension Runs" table for `entire search --json`, `entire auth status --json`, and `entire graph version --json`, plus a paragraph on setup commands, which run only in a terminal, only on a click.
  - Rewrite the read-only paragraph and the Limits bullet at line 110.
  - Add the `entire.search.hosted` setting.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md:**
  - Update the invariants: nothing reads the network or runs a brain command until the Brain, Trails, Sessions, or Setup view is on screen, or you search.
  - Setup commands run only through `setupTerminal.ts`.
  - The Setup page is scriptless, like the Brain page.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** Add an entry. Don't bump the version unless asked.
- Write the prose in the house style (the entire-elements-of-style skill): title-case headings, no em dashes.

## Tests

- **Unit (vitest):**
  - `test/unit/search.test.ts`: `readSearchPage` on the real fixtures captured above (a commit with a trailer, a session with `matchedCheckpointId`, `pr` and `repo` skipped, malformed input → undefined), `matchesLocal`, and `trailMatches`.
  - `test/unit/entireCli.test.ts`:
    - `search` args put `--` before the query, a bad query is rejected without running, and stderr "not logged in" maps to `notLoggedIn`.
    - `authStatus` parsing.
    - `graphVersion` maps a missing plugin to `pluginMissing`.
  - `test/unit/setup.test.ts`: `setupSteps` for each fact combination (CLI missing blocks everything, Connect hidden without `entireRepo`, Connect blocked without login), plus `setupCommandLine` quoting on POSIX and Windows and with paths containing spaces or quotes.
  - `test/webview/setupPage.test.ts`: escaping, and that the page links only to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- **Extension host:**
  - Add `search`, `auth status --json`, and `graph version --json` replies to the scenarios in `.vscode-test.mjs`.
  - New `test/integration/search.test.cjs` (added to a config's `files`):
    - Local hits appear without a CLI call.
    - Entire's hits merge and deduplicate.
    - Accepting a session hit opens the panel on `matchedCheckpointId`.
    - `notLoggedIn` gives the login hint.
    - No `search` call runs until search is used.
  - New `test/integration/setup.test.cjs`:
    - In the `not-enabled` and `cli-missing` launches, `entire.showSetup` is true and the page lists the right steps.
    - `entire.runSetupStep` opens a terminal named "Entire Setup".
    - After the scenario flips `status --json` to enabled and Check Again runs, the view state becomes `ready`.
  - Extend `test/integration/states.test.cjs` so `auth status`, `graph version`, and `search` never run while the sidebar stays closed.
  - Update `test/integration/brain.test.cjs` for the new primary button.

## Verification

1. `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, unit tests).
2. `npm run test:host` (extension-host tests, including the new search and setup suites).
3. Manual run in the Extension Development Host (F5):
   - In this repository (enabled, `entire://`, logged in), Search finds "homepage" (commit b83de22 and session d549f207) and opens each in the detail panel. The Trails search finds `#2923`.
   - In a scratch git repository with Entire not enabled, the Setup page shows. Enable runs `entire enable` in the terminal, and when it ends the views turn to ready without a manual refresh. Graph and Brain install and set up, and Connect shows only for an `entire://` origin.
   - Point `entire.cliPath` at a missing file. The Setup page shows the CLI step, the install Quick Pick lists this platform's commands, and Set Path still works.
4. `npm run smoke -- .` to confirm nothing regressed in the data path.

Opening the sidebar in `not-enabled` also shows Trails (`hasTrails` is true there), which runs `trail list` and breaks the "sidebar never opened" premise (`states.test.cjs:18-19`). Give it its own launch, scenario file and log.
   - `runSetupStep` would really run the command in a terminal: `entire enable` against the fake CLI, or `brew`/`curl` for the CLI step. Make the terminal runner replaceable, the way `brain.openUrl` is (`brainService.ts:59`).

### Medium

4. **More brain tests break than the plan lists.** Besides `brain.test.cjs:288-291`, `test/webview/brainPage.test.ts:93,101` assert the exact buttons, and `:148` asserts that every command in `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS` is used.

5. **Login has no follow-up refresh.** `reload({manual:false})` re-reads trails and Entire's session list only on a manual reload (`repoManager.ts:426-433, 446`). After the Login step, call `loadTrails` and `loadRemoteSessions` for repos whose `failure.kind === 'notLoggedIn'`. Otherwise "loggedOut" and `sessionsNotice()` stay on screen.

6. **Gate hosted search on `repo.entireRepo`.** README:79 promises network calls only for `entire://` origins, and the plan gates only on the setting.

7. **Local session data is thinner than the plan assumes.**
   - `sessions(repo)` returns `{active, recent}`, not a flat list.
   - Names (`remoteSessions`) and `lastPrompt` (`sessionRows`) stay unset until the Sessions view is shown (`repoManager.ts:213-214`, `extension.ts:98-107`).
   - `branch` is set only for active sessions (`:1081`).
   - Also match `entry.title` and `repo.index.allRows()` messages; the CLI's checkpoint rows cover checkpoints on other branches.
   - Never call `loadSessionRows` from search, because it prunes session state.

8. **Quick Pick ordering.** `sortByLabel` isn't in the stable 1.95 typings. With a non-empty value, VS Code re-sorts items by label match, and `alwaysShow` doesn't stop that. Separators probably stop rendering while you type (I couldn't confirm this from source). Don't rely on separator groups or Entire's ranking surviving; put the kind in the codicon or description, and check this early in F5.

9. **`entire.openSetup` race.** `setContext` is fire-and-forget throughout (`repoManager.ts:1230`), and `<view>.focus` on a hidden view rejects (`trails.test.cjs:801` swallows exactly that). Await `setContext` before `entire.setup.focus` and tolerate a rejection.

### Low

10. **No new BrainService API is needed.** `loadStatus(repo)` is public (`brainService.ts:138`), along with `details(root)` (`:96`), `stateOf` (`:112`), `ensureStatus()` (`:123`, enabled repos only) and `onDidChange`.

11. **The CLI-missing and too-old states leave repo facts unset.** In those states `loadStatus` never runs, so `repo.entireRepo` and `repo.status` are undefined. Enable and Connect must render as blocked or unknown, never "needed".

12. **Manifest details.**
    - The wrapper commands need their own `$(search)` icon, because `view/title` shows the wrapper's icon.
    - Gate the Checkpoints and Sessions search buttons on `entire.viewState == 'ready'`.
    - The extension activates only on views and commands (`package.json:51-54`). A palette `when` on keys it sets hides Search until the sidebar has been opened once. Give `entire.openSetup` no `when`.

13. **Small fixes.**
    - `SESSION_ID` isn't exported (`entireCli.ts:51`).
    - `relativeTime` takes milliseconds, but `CommitRecord.authorTime` is in seconds (`trailers.ts:39`).
    - `showCommitDiff` on a commit missing from the clone says "changed no files" (`actions.ts:80-82`). Check `git.commit(root, sha)` first.
    - The docs URL is `docs.entire.io` (`commands.ts:16`), not `docs.entire.com`.
    - `& '…'` quoting works only in PowerShell. Choose it from `vscode.env.shell`, not the platform.
    - `runSetupStep` should check `root` with `manager.repoFor` and `stepId` against the step enum.

- `manager.detail` uses `explainCheckpoint`, which asks the remote (`repoManager.ts:998-1012`).

- `isPluginMissing` is at `brain.ts:240`.
- Shell-integration APIs are in the 1.95 typings.
- `views.entire.at(-1)` stays Brain (`brain.test.cjs:96`), so putting Setup first doesn't break that test.
