input.content:
# Search and Entire Setup for the VS Code Extension

## Context

The extension lists checkpoints, sessions, and trails, but it can't search them, so the only way to find one is to scroll. And when Entire isn't set up in a repository, the views show a sentence and a Copy Command button for each missing piece. Graph and Brain Connect aren't covered at all.

This change adds two features:

1. **Search.** An `Entire: Search` Quick Pick that searches as you type. A search button in each view's title bar opens it limited to that view.
2. **Entire Setup.** A Setup page in the sidebar: a live checklist of CLI, Login, Enable, Graph, Brain, and Brain Connect. Each step's button runs its command in an integrated terminal, and the page checks the step again when the command ends.

Decisions you made during planning:
- Setup commands run in an integrated terminal.
- Setup lives on a sidebar Setup page.
- Search is a Quick Pick plus a button on each view.

This reverses the README's statement that the extension "does not run `entire enable` for you" and does not install or build the brain. Setup commands still run only in a visible terminal, and only when you click a step, so the README and CONTRIBUTING change to say that.

## What the CLI Provides

I checked these against CLI 0.13.4, graph v0.6.0, and brain v0.5.1.

### Search

`entire search --json --limit N -- <query>` takes about 2 seconds and needs a login. It searches the current repository by default, and `--` keeps a query that starts with `-` from being read as a flag.

The output is `{results:[{type,data,searchMeta}], total, page, total_pages, counts}`, and `type` is one of `commit|session|checkpoint|pr|repo`:
- **Commit hits:** `commitSha`, `commitSubject`, `commitMessage` (which carries the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer), `branch`, `author`, `createdAt`.
- **Session hits:** `sessionId`, `matchedCheckpointId`, `displayName`, `prompt`, `agent`, `branch`, `createdAt`, and `searchMeta.snippet`.
- **Checkpoint hits:** none appeared in testing, so the reader handles them defensively.

### Trails

There is no trail search command. Trails are matched on the client against `entire trail list --json` with no `--status`, which lists all of them.

### Status Checks

- `entire auth status --json` returns `{logged_in, user, …}` in about 0.9 seconds.
- `entire graph version --json` exits 0 when the Graph plugin is installed, in about 0.1 seconds. When it isn't installed, the CLI prints its usage and `unknown command`.
- `entire graph setup` writes `.entire/agent-guide.md` and a managed `<!-- entire-agent:begin -->` block in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- `entire brain status --json` already gives `manifest_state`, `hosted.state`, and `hosted.synced`, through `readBrainStatus` in `src/core/brain.ts:70`.
- `entire brain connect` needs a login and resolves the repository through `entire repo view`.

### Plugins and Install

- The plugin index names are `graph` and `brain`.
- Install commands:
  - macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`, or the install script.
  - Linux: `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash`.
  - Windows: `irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex`.
- Keep `INSTALL_URL` at docs.entire.io (`commands.ts:16`), which redirects.

## Part 1: Search

### Core: `src/core/search.ts` (New, No `vscode` Import)

**Hit types.** A `SearchHit` union:
- `{kind:'commit', sha, subject, checkpointIds, branch?, author?, createdAt?}`. The checkpoint IDs come from `parseCheckpointIds` in `src/core/trailers.ts:26`.
- `{kind:'session', sessionId, checkpointId?, name, prompt?, agent?, branch?, createdAt?, snippet?}`.
- `{kind:'checkpoint', checkpointId, …}`.

**Reader.** `readSearchPage(value)` is a hand-written reader in the style of `schemas.ts`:
- It skips `pr` hits, `repo` hits, and malformed hits.
- It checks IDs with `isCheckpointId` and the session ID pattern. Move `SESSION_ID` out of `entireCli.ts:51`, where it isn't exported, into a shared module.

**Matching.**
- `isSearchQuery(text)` accepts 1 to 500 characters with no control characters.
- `matchesLocal(query, fields)`: every word must appear in some field, case-insensitive. Words of the form `x:y` are left out, except `branch:x`, which filters on the branch.
- `trailMatches(query, trail)` matches `#123` or `123` against the trail number, and words against the title, body, phase, and branch names.

### CLI: `src/core/entireCli.ts`

`search(cwd, query, limit, signal)` runs `['search','--json','--limit',N,'--',query]`.
- Timeout: 30 seconds.
- Failure wording: `remote: true`, so the call maps failures to `notLoggedIn` and `noAccess`.
- It rejects a query that fails `isSearchQuery` before running anything.

### Quick Pick: `src/ext/searchPicker.ts` (New)

`entire.search(scope?)`, where `scope` is `'checkpoints'|'sessions'|'trails'`, uses `createQuickPick`, following `pickTrailFilter` (`commands.ts:96`).

**Local results** draw at once, from data that is already loaded and without running any CLI command:
- Checkpoints:
  - Commits in `repo.index`: subject, SHA, checkpoint IDs.
  - The CLI's checkpoint rows. These cover checkpoints on other branches; verify the accessor in `checkpointIndex.ts` (`allRows()` or `unlinkedRows()`).
- Sessions:
  - Every entry of `manager.sessions(repo)`, which returns `{active, recent}`.
  - Fields matched: `name`, `title`, `opening`, `lastPrompt`, ID, `agent`, and `branch`.
  - Names and last prompts may be unset until the Sessions view has been shown. Never call `loadSessionRows` from search, because it prunes session state.
- Trails: `repo.trails`, when already read.

**Entire's search** adds hits after that:
- It runs only for repositories with `repo.entireRepo`, which keeps the README's promise that only `entire://` origins reach the network, and only while `entire.search.hosted` is on.
- It runs for the checkpoint and session scopes.
- It is debounced 300 ms, shows `busy`, and aborts the previous query with an `AbortController`.
- It needs at least 2 characters.

**Trails** are read once per picker:
- It runs for each repository in `manager.trailRepos` (`repoManager.ts:532`, which already applies the trails setting and view state).
- Read page 1 with `manager.cli.listTrails(root, {project: trailProject(r), repo: trailRepo(r)}, 'all', PAGE_SIZE)` and add it to a fresh `TrailPages` with `addTrailPage`.
- Then call `readTrailPages(list, fetch, () => false, {maxPages: 3})` (`trails.ts:126`) and match with `trailMatches`.

**Merging.**
- Deduplicate by checkpoint ID, session ID, and SHA.
- Every item has `alwaysShow: true`.
- Each item names its kind in its codicon (`$(git-commit)`, `$(comment-discussion)`, `$(milestone)`) and in its description.
- **Risk to check first in F5:** the stable 1.95 API has no `sortByLabel`, so VS Code may re-sort items by how well their labels match, and hide separators while you type. If that scrambles Entire's ranking, the fallback is a two-step flow: an input box for the query, then a results Quick Pick with an empty value.

**Items.**
- **Label:** the title.
- **Description:** branch, agent, and relative time.
  - `relativeTime` takes milliseconds, but `CommitRecord.authorTime` is in seconds, so multiply it by 1,000.
- **Detail:** the snippet on one line, at most 120 characters.
- **Buttons:**
  - Open in New Tab.
  - Open on entire.com, when the repository has an `entireRepo`.

**Hint items:**
- `notLoggedIn`: "Log in to Entire to search sessions on Entire". This runs the Setup Login step.
- `noAccess`: "Entire does not know this repository".
- Any other failure: "Search on Entire failed", which opens Show Log.

**Accepting an item:**
- **Commit or checkpoint with a checkpoint ID:** `panels.open({repoRoot, mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId, commitSha}, {newTab})`. The panel loads through `manager.detail`, which fetches from the checkpoint remote when needed.
- **Commit with no checkpoint:** if `git.commit(root, sha)` finds it in the clone, use `actions.showCommitDiff`. Otherwise open it on the web. `showCommitDiff` on a commit that isn't in the clone would wrongly say it changed no files (`actions.ts:80`).
- **Session the merged list knows:** `{mode:'session', sessionId}`.
- **Session the list doesn't know:** `{mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId: matchedCheckpointId, sessionId}`, which preselects the slot (`panelController.ts:434`). Session mode would say "no record" (`:422`). With no checkpoint ID, open it on the web.
- **Trail:** `panels.openTrail({repoRoot, mode:'trail', trail: number, id})`.

**Empty query.** List the newest local sessions and checkpoint commits.

**Multi-root.** Show the repository name in the description.

### Search Manifest

- **`entire.search`.** Command "Search", icon `$(search)`, with **no** palette `when`. The extension activates on its commands, and a `when` on its own context keys would hide Search until the sidebar has been opened once. When nothing is ready, the handler offers Set Up Entire.
- **Wrapper commands.** `entire.searchCheckpoints`, `entire.searchSessions`, and `entire.searchTrails`, each with its own `$(search)` icon and hidden from the palette. `view/title` items pass no arguments, so each view needs its own command.
- **Title-bar buttons.** On `navigation@0`:
  - Checkpoints and Sessions show theirs when `entire.viewState == 'ready'`.
  - Trails shows its button whenever the view is shown.
- **Setting.** `entire.search.hosted`, default `true`.

## Part 2: Entire Setup

### Steps

| Step | Done When | Runs in the Terminal | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | View state is past `cliMissing` and `cliTooOld` | A Quick Pick of this platform's install methods, each showing its exact command, plus Open Installation Docs. For a CLI that is too old, the upgrade path: Homebrew if the binary is under a Homebrew prefix, otherwise the script. | Nothing |
| Login | `entire auth status --json` reports `logged_in` | `entire login` | CLI |
| Enable | `repo.enabled` | `entire enable` (interactive) | CLI |
| Graph | The plugin answers `graph version`, and `.entire/agent-guide.md` exists and mentions `entire graph` | `entire plugin install graph`, then `entire graph setup` | CLI |
| Brain | `brainStatus` is not `pluginMissing`, and `manifest_state !== 'absent'` | `entire plugin install brain`, then `entire brain setup` | CLI |
| Brain Connect | Applies only when `repo.entireRepo` is set. Done when `hosted.state === 'connected'`. | `entire brain connect` | Login, a built brain |

- CLI and Enable are required. Login is recommended, because search, trails, session names, and Connect need it. Graph, Brain, and Connect are optional.
- CLI and Login apply to the whole machine. The other steps are listed for each repository.
- **CLI missing or too old.** `loadStatus` never runs in these states, so `repo.entireRepo` and `repo.status` are unknown. Enable, Graph, Brain, and Connect then show as blocked with the reason "Needs the Entire CLI", never as needed.

### Core

**`src/core/setup.ts` (new):**
- Types: `SetupStepId`, `SetupFacts`, and `setupSteps(facts) → SetupStepView[]`.
  - Each step's state is `done|needed|optional|blocked|running|unknown`, with a reason and its actions.
- `setupCommandLine(action, cli, shellKind)`:
  - The program is bare `entire` when the CLI was found on `PATH`. Otherwise it is the quoted located path: single quotes for POSIX shells, `& '…'` for PowerShell, `"…"` for cmd.
  - Only constant arguments follow the program.
  - The caller picks the shell kind from `vscode.env.shell`, not from the platform.
- `installOptions(platform, hasBrew, cliPath?)`.

**`src/core/pageKit.ts` (new).** Move `escapeHtml`, `commandHref`, `button`, and the base `STYLES` out of `brainPage.ts`. `brainPage.ts` re-exports `escapeHtml`.

**`src/core/setupPage.ts` (new):**
- Exports `setupPageHtml(model, nonce)` and `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- The page has no script, uses the Brain page's CSP, and escapes all text. Its buttons are command links with `[root, stepId]` arguments.
- Each row has:
  - A status: ✓ Done, Needed, Optional, Running in terminal…, or Needs ….
  - A title.
  - One sentence on what the step gives you.
  - A button.
- The footer has Check Again and Hide Setup. When everything is done, the page says so and keeps Hide Setup.

**`src/core/schemas.ts`.** Add `readAuthStatus`, which reads `logged_in` and `user`.

**`src/core/entireCli.ts`:**
- `authStatus(cwd)`: runs `auth status --json` with a 15-second timeout and `dedupe`.
- `graphVersion(cwd)`: runs `graph version --json` with a 5-second timeout. Generalize `isPluginMissing` (`brain.ts:240`) to take the plugin name, so that `unknown command "graph` maps to `pluginMissing`.

### Extension

**`src/ext/setupTerminal.ts` (new).** A `SetupRunner` interface with one implementation, the default terminal runner.
- `run(root, label, commandLine)` resolves to `{exitCode?}`.
- It uses one terminal for each repository root, named "Entire Setup", with `cwd: root`.
- If shell integration comes up within 5 seconds (`terminal.shellIntegration` or `onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration`, both in the 1.95 typings):
  - It runs `shellIntegration.executeCommand(commandLine)`.
  - It resolves on `window.onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` for that execution.
- Otherwise:
  - It uses `sendText`.
  - It resolves at once, and the page says "Running in terminal. Click Check Again when it finishes."
  - The service also checks again when the terminal closes and when the window regains focus.
- The runner can be replaced through the test API, the way `brain.openUrl` is (`brainService.ts:59`), so the host tests never run `entire enable`, `brew`, or `curl` for real.

**`src/ext/setupService.ts` (new).**
- It holds `SetupFacts` and the step running in each repository, and fires `onDidChange`.

`refresh()`:
- Reads, in parallel:
  - `authStatus` and `graphVersion`.
  - The guide file.
  - The brain, through the existing public `brain.loadStatus(repo)`, `details(root)`, and `stateOf(root)` (`brainService.ts:96,112,138`). No new BrainService API is needed.
- Runs only while the Setup view is visible.

`runStep(root, stepId)`:
- Checks `root` with `manager.repoFor` and `stepId` against the step enum.
- Builds the command line, marks the step running, waits for the runner, then refreshes.
- After the CLI or Enable step, it runs `manager.reload({manual:false})`.
- After the Login step, it runs `entire.refresh`. A manual reload is the only thing that reads trails and Entire's session list again (`repoManager.ts:426-433, 446`), so this clears `loggedOut` and the sessions login notice.
- After a Brain step, it runs `brain.refresh()`.

`entire.showSetup` is true when either of these holds:
- `viewState` is `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, or `notEnabled`.
- Setup is pinned. Setup becomes pinned the first time the Setup view is shown in a state that isn't ready, when `entire.openSetup` runs, or when a step runs. The pin is stored in `workspaceState` and cleared only by Hide Setup.

Without the pin, a successful Enable would switch the state to `ready` and hide the page before Graph, Brain, and Connect were done.

**`src/ext/views/setupView.ts` (new).**
- A `WebviewViewProvider` modeled on `BrainView` (`views/brainView.ts`).
- Options: `enableScripts:false`, and `enableCommandUris` set to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- It redraws only when the HTML changes.
- It calls `setup.refresh()` on the first resolve and each time it becomes visible.

**`src/ext/repoManager.ts`.** Store `cliPath` and `cliSource` from `located` (`:386`) before the version check, and clear them when nothing is located.

**`src/ext/commands.ts`:**
- `entire.openSetup`: await `setContext('entire.showSetup', true)`, then run `entire.setup.focus`, and tolerate a rejection.
- New commands:
  - `entire.runSetupStep(root, stepId)`
  - `entire.checkSetup`
  - `entire.hideSetup`
- `entire.installCli` opens the install Quick Pick.
- The copy commands stay registered and stay hidden.

**`src/core/brainPage.ts`.** The `pluginMissing` and `noBrain` notices get a primary Run in Terminal button that calls `entire.runSetupStep`, and keep Copy Command as a secondary button. Add `entire.runSetupStep` to `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`.

**`src/extension.ts`:**
- Wire up the setup service, the runner, the setup view, and the search picker.
- Register the `entire.setup` view.
- Extend `EntireTestApi` with:
  - `setup`: facts, `showSetup`, the last page HTML, and a replaceable `runner`.
  - `search(query, scope)`, which returns the items.
  - `acceptSearch(item)`.

### Setup Manifest

- **The `entire.setup` webview view.** Named "Setup", first in the `entire` container, with `when: entire.showSetup`.
- **`viewsWelcome`.** For `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, and `notEnabled` on Checkpoints and Sessions: one sentence plus `[Set Up Entire](command:entire.openSetup)` and Retry.
- **`entire.openSetup`.** "Set Up Entire", in the palette with no `when`, and in the Checkpoints title overflow menu.
- **Hidden commands.** `runSetupStep`, `checkSetup`, and `hideSetup` stay out of the palette.

## Docs

**README.md:**
- Add Search and Setup sections.
- Change Getting Started to: open the Entire view and follow Setup.
- In the What the Extension Runs table:
  - Add `entire search --json` (when you search, `entire://` origins only).
  - Add `entire auth status --json` and `entire graph version --json` (while the Setup page is on screen).
  - Add a paragraph saying setup commands run only in a terminal when you click a step.
- Rewrite the read-only paragraph and the Limits bullet at line 110.
- Add `entire.search.hosted`.

**CONTRIBUTING.md:**
- Invariants: nothing reads the network or runs a brain or plugin command until the Brain, Trails, Sessions, or Setup view is on screen, or you search.
- Setup commands go only through `SetupRunner`.
- The Setup page has no script and its command links are allowlisted.

**CHANGELOG.md.** Add an entry. Leave the version as is.

Write all prose in the house style (the entire-elements-of-style skill).

## Tests

### Unit (vitest)

- `test/unit/search.test.ts`:
  - `readSearchPage` on the captured real hits: a commit with a trailer, and a session with `matchedCheckpointId`.
  - `pr` and `repo` hits are skipped, and malformed output gives `undefined`.
  - `matchesLocal` and `trailMatches`.
- `test/unit/entireCli.test.ts`:
  - `search` puts `--` before the query, and a bad query runs nothing.
  - "not logged in" gives `notLoggedIn`.
  - `authStatus` parses.
  - `graphVersion` with no plugin gives `pluginMissing`.
- `test/unit/setup.test.ts`:
  - `setupSteps` across fact combinations: CLI missing blocks the rest, Connect is hidden without `entireRepo`, and Connect is blocked without a login.
  - The pinned behavior.
  - `setupCommandLine` quoting for POSIX, PowerShell, and cmd, including paths with spaces or quotes.
- `test/webview/setupPage.test.ts`: escaping, and that the page links only to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- `test/webview/brainPage.test.ts`: update the button assertions at `:93` and `:101`. The check at `:148` that every allowlisted command is used must still pass.

### Extension Host

- **Scenarios in `.vscode-test.mjs`:**
  - Add `search`, `auth status --json`, and `graph version --json` replies to the healthy scenario.
  - Add a new `setup` launch with its own scenario file and `FAKE_ENTIRE_LOG`, starting not enabled. Don't reuse the `not-enabled` or `cli-missing` launches. `states.test.cjs` relies on their sidebar staying closed, and opening it would also read trails.
- **`test/integration/search.test.cjs` (new):**
  - Local hits come with no CLI call.
  - Entire's hits merge and are deduplicated.
  - A session hit opens on `matchedCheckpointId`.
  - `notLoggedIn` gives the login hint.
  - No `search` call runs until search is used.
- **`test/integration/setup.test.cjs` (new):**
  - `showSetup` (from the test API) is true, and the page lists the expected steps.
  - With a stub runner, `runSetupStep(root,'enable')` records `entire enable`.
  - After the scenario flips `status --json` to enabled and the runner resolves, `viewState` becomes `ready` and the page stays shown because it is pinned.
  - Hide Setup clears the pin.
- **`test/integration/states.test.cjs`.** Assert from memory that the setup facts are unset and its HTML is `''` while the sidebar stays closed, as the existing invariants do (`:21-33`).
- **`test/integration/brain.test.cjs`.** Update `:288-291` for the new primary button.

## Verification

1. `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, unit tests).
2. `npm run test:host`.

# Search and Entire Setup for the VS Code Extension

## Context

The extension lists checkpoints, sessions, and trails, but it can't search them, so the only way to find one is to scroll. And when Entire isn't set up in a repository, the views show a sentence and a Copy Command button for each missing piece. Graph and Brain Connect aren't covered at all.

This change adds two features:

1. **Search.** An `Entire: Search` Quick Pick that searches as you type. A search button in each view's title bar opens it limited to that view.
2. **Entire Setup.** A Setup page in the sidebar: a live checklist of CLI, Login, Enable, Graph, Brain, and Brain Connect. Each step's button runs its command in an integrated terminal, and the page checks the step again when the command ends.

Decisions you made during planning:
- Setup commands run in an integrated terminal.
- Setup lives on a sidebar Setup page.
- Search is a Quick Pick plus a button on each view.

This reverses the README's statement that the extension "does not run `entire enable` for you" and does not install or build the brain. Setup commands still run only in a visible terminal, and only when you click a step, so the README and CONTRIBUTING change to say that.

## What the CLI Provides

I checked these against CLI 0.13.4, graph v0.6.0, and brain v0.5.1.

### Search

`entire search --json --limit N -- <query>` takes about 2 seconds and needs a login. It searches the current repository by default, and `--` keeps a query that starts with `-` from being read as a flag.

The output is `{results:[{type,data,searchMeta}], total, page, total_pages, counts}`, and `type` is one of `commit|session|checkpoint|pr|repo`:
- **Commit hits:** `commitSha`, `commitSubject`, `commitMessage` (which carries the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer), `branch`, `author`, `createdAt`.
- **Session hits:** `sessionId`, `matchedCheckpointId`, `displayName`, `prompt`, `agent`, `branch`, `createdAt`, and `searchMeta.snippet`.
- **Checkpoint hits:** none appeared in testing, so the reader handles them defensively.

### Trails

There is no trail search command. Trails are matched on the client against `entire trail list --json` with no `--status`, which lists all of them.

### Status Checks

- `entire auth status --json` returns `{logged_in, user, …}` in about 0.9 seconds.
- `entire graph version --json` exits 0 when the Graph plugin is installed, in about 0.1 seconds. When it isn't installed, the CLI prints its usage and `unknown command`.
- `entire graph setup` writes `.entire/agent-guide.md` and a managed `<!-- entire-agent:begin -->` block in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- `entire brain status --json` already gives `manifest_state`, `hosted.state`, and `hosted.synced`, through `readBrainStatus` in `src/core/brain.ts:70`.
- `entire brain connect` needs a login and resolves the repository through `entire repo view`.

### Plugins and Install

- The plugin index names are `graph` and `brain`.
- Install commands:
  - macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`, or the install script.
  - Linux: `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash`.
  - Windows: `irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex`.
- Keep `INSTALL_URL` at docs.entire.io (`commands.ts:16`), which redirects.

## Part 1: Search

### Core: `src/core/search.ts` (New, No `vscode` Import)

**Hit types.** A `SearchHit` union:
- `{kind:'commit', sha, subject, checkpointIds, branch?, author?, createdAt?}`. The checkpoint IDs come from `parseCheckpointIds` in `src/core/trailers.ts:26`.
- `{kind:'session', sessionId, checkpointId?, name, prompt?, agent?, branch?, createdAt?, snippet?}`.
- `{kind:'checkpoint', checkpointId, …}`.

**Reader.** `readSearchPage(value)` is a hand-written reader in the style of `schemas.ts`:
- It skips `pr` hits, `repo` hits, and malformed hits.
- It checks IDs with `isCheckpointId` and the session ID pattern. Move `SESSION_ID` out of `entireCli.ts:51`, where it isn't exported, into a shared module.

**Matching.**
- `isSearchQuery(text)` accepts 1 to 500 characters with no control characters.
- `matchesLocal(query, fields)`: every word must appear in some field, case-insensitive. Words of the form `x:y` are left out, except `branch:x`, which filters on the branch.
- `trailMatches(query, trail)` matches `#123` or `123` against the trail number, and words against the title, body, phase, and branch names.

### CLI: `src/core/entireCli.ts`

`search(cwd, query, limit, signal)` runs `['search','--json','--limit',N,'--',query]`.
- Timeout: 30 seconds.
- Failure wording: `remote: true`, so the call maps failures to `notLoggedIn` and `noAccess`.
- It rejects a query that fails `isSearchQuery` before running anything.

### Quick Pick: `src/ext/searchPicker.ts` (New)

`entire.search(scope?)`, where `scope` is `'checkpoints'|'sessions'|'trails'`, uses `createQuickPick`, following `pickTrailFilter` (`commands.ts:96`).

**Local results** draw at once, from data that is already loaded and without running any CLI command:
- Checkpoints:
  - Commits in `repo.index`: subject, SHA, checkpoint IDs.
  - The CLI's checkpoint rows. These cover checkpoints on other branches; verify the accessor in `checkpointIndex.ts` (`allRows()` or `unlinkedRows()`).
- Sessions:
  - Every entry of `manager.sessions(repo)`, which returns `{active, recent}`.
  - Fields matched: `name`, `title`, `opening`, `lastPrompt`, ID, `agent`, and `branch`.
  - Names and last prompts may be unset until the Sessions view has been shown. Never call `loadSessionRows` from search, because it prunes session state.
- Trails: `repo.trails`, when already read.

**Entire's search** adds hits after that:
- It runs only for repositories with `repo.entireRepo`, which keeps the README's promise that only `entire://` origins reach the network, and only while `entire.search.hosted` is on.
- It runs for the checkpoint and session scopes.
- It is debounced 300 ms, shows `busy`, and aborts the previous query with an `AbortController`.
- It needs at least 2 characters.

**Trails** are read once per picker:
- It runs for each repository in `manager.trailRepos` (`repoManager.ts:532`, which already applies the trails setting and view state).
- Read page 1 with `manager.cli.listTrails(root, {project: trailProject(r), repo: trailRepo(r)}, 'all', PAGE_SIZE)` and add it to a fresh `TrailPages` with `addTrailPage`.
- Then call `readTrailPages(list, fetch, () => false, {maxPages: 3})` (`trails.ts:126`) and match with `trailMatches`.

**Merging.**
- Deduplicate by checkpoint ID, session ID, and SHA.
- Every item has `alwaysShow: true`.
- Each item names its kind in its codicon (`$(git-commit)`, `$(comment-discussion)`, `$(milestone)`) and in its description.
- **Risk to check first in F5:** the stable 1.95 API has no `sortByLabel`, so VS Code may re-sort items by how well their labels match, and hide separators while you type. If that scrambles Entire's ranking, the fallback is a two-step flow: an input box for the query, then a results Quick Pick with an empty value.

**Items.**
- **Label:** the title.
- **Description:** branch, agent, and relative time.
  - `relativeTime` takes milliseconds, but `CommitRecord.authorTime` is in seconds, so multiply it by 1,000.
- **Detail:** the snippet on one line, at most 120 characters.
- **Buttons:**
  - Open in New Tab.
  - Open on entire.com, when the repository has an `entireRepo`.

**Hint items:**
- `notLoggedIn`: "Log in to Entire to search sessions on Entire". This runs the Setup Login step.
- `noAccess`: "Entire does not know this repository".
- Any other failure: "Search on Entire failed", which opens Show Log.

**Accepting an item:**
- **Commit or checkpoint with a checkpoint ID:** `panels.open({repoRoot, mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId, commitSha}, {newTab})`. The panel loads through `manager.detail`, which fetches from the checkpoint remote when needed.
- **Commit with no checkpoint:** if `git.commit(root, sha)` finds it in the clone, use `actions.showCommitDiff`. Otherwise open it on the web. `showCommitDiff` on a commit that isn't in the clone would wrongly say it changed no files (`actions.ts:80`).
- **Session the merged list knows:** `{mode:'session', sessionId}`.
- **Session the list doesn't know:** `{mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId: matchedCheckpointId, sessionId}`, which preselects the slot (`panelController.ts:434`). Session mode would say "no record" (`:422`). With no checkpoint ID, open it on the web.
- **Trail:** `panels.openTrail({repoRoot, mode:'trail', trail: number, id})`.

**Empty query.** List the newest local sessions and checkpoint commits.

**Multi-root.** Show the repository name in the description.

### Search Manifest

- **`entire.search`.** Command "Search", icon `$(search)`, with **no** palette `when`. The extension activates on its commands, and a `when` on its own context keys would hide Search until the sidebar has been opened once. When nothing is ready, the handler offers Set Up Entire.
- **Wrapper commands.** `entire.searchCheckpoints`, `entire.searchSessions`, and `entire.searchTrails`, each with its own `$(search)` icon and hidden from the palette. `view/title` items pass no arguments, so each view needs its own command.
- **Title-bar buttons.** On `navigation@0`:
  - Checkpoints and Sessions show theirs when `entire.viewState == 'ready'`.
  - Trails shows its button whenever the view is shown.
- **Setting.** `entire.search.hosted`, default `true`.

## Part 2: Entire Setup

### Steps

| Step | Done When | Runs in the Terminal | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | View state is past `cliMissing` and `cliTooOld` | A Quick Pick of this platform's install methods, each showing its exact command, plus Open Installation Docs. For a CLI that is too old, the upgrade path: Homebrew if the binary is under a Homebrew prefix, otherwise the script. | Nothing |
| Login | `entire auth status --json` reports `logged_in` | `entire login` | CLI |
| Enable | `repo.enabled` | `entire enable` (interactive) | CLI |
| Graph | The plugin answers `graph version`, and `.entire/agent-guide.md` exists and mentions `entire graph` | `entire plugin install graph`, then `entire graph setup` | CLI |
| Brain | `brainStatus` is not `pluginMissing`, and `manifest_state !== 'absent'` | `entire plugin install brain`, then `entire brain setup` | CLI |
| Brain Connect | Applies only when `repo.entireRepo` is set. Done when `hosted.state === 'connected'`. | `entire brain connect` | Login, a built brain |

- CLI and Enable are required. Login is recommended, because search, trails, session names, and Connect need it. Graph, Brain, and Connect are optional.
- CLI and Login apply to the whole machine. The other steps are listed for each repository.
- **CLI missing or too old.** `loadStatus` never runs in these states, so `repo.entireRepo` and `repo.status` are unknown. Enable, Graph, Brain, and Connect then show as blocked with the reason "Needs the Entire CLI", never as needed.

### Core

**`src/core/setup.ts` (new):**
- Types: `SetupStepId`, `SetupFacts`, and `setupSteps(facts) → SetupStepView[]`.
  - Each step's state is `done|needed|optional|blocked|running|unknown`, with a reason and its actions.
- `setupCommandLine(action, cli, shellKind)`:
  - The program is bare `entire` when the CLI was found on `PATH`. Otherwise it is the quoted located path: single quotes for POSIX shells, `& '…'` for PowerShell, `"…"` for cmd.
  - Only constant arguments follow the program.
  - The caller picks the shell kind from `vscode.env.shell`, not from the platform.
- `installOptions(platform, hasBrew, cliPath?)`.

**`src/core/pageKit.ts` (new).** Move `escapeHtml`, `commandHref`, `button`, and the base `STYLES` out of `brainPage.ts`. `brainPage.ts` re-exports `escapeHtml`.

**`src/core/setupPage.ts` (new):**
- Exports `setupPageHtml(model, nonce)` and `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- The page has no script, uses the Brain page's CSP, and escapes all text. Its buttons are command links with `[root, stepId]` arguments.
- Each row has:
  - A status: ✓ Done, Needed, Optional, Running in terminal…, or Needs ….
  - A title.
  - One sentence on what the step gives you.
  - A button.
- The footer has Check Again and Hide Setup. When everything is done, the page says so and keeps Hide Setup.

**`src/core/schemas.ts`.** Add `readAuthStatus`, which reads `logged_in` and `user`.

**`src/core/entireCli.ts`:**
- `authStatus(cwd)`: runs `auth status --json` with a 15-second timeout and `dedupe`.
- `graphVersion(cwd)`: runs `graph version --json` with a 5-second timeout. Generalize `isPluginMissing` (`brain.ts:240`) to take the plugin name, so that `unknown command "graph` maps to `pluginMissing`.

### Extension

**`src/ext/setupTerminal.ts` (new).** A `SetupRunner` interface with one implementation, the default terminal runner.
- `run(root, label, commandLine)` resolves to `{exitCode?}`.
- It uses one terminal for each repository root, named "Entire Setup", with `cwd: root`.
- If shell integration comes up within 5 seconds (`terminal.shellIntegration` or `onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration`, both in the 1.95 typings):
  - It runs `shellIntegration.executeCommand(commandLine)`.
  - It resolves on `window.onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` for that execution.
- Otherwise:
  - It uses `sendText`.
  - It resolves at once, and the page says "Running in terminal. Click Check Again when it finishes."
  - The service also checks again when the terminal closes and when the window regains focus.
- The runner can be replaced through the test API, the way `brain.openUrl` is (`brainService.ts:59`), so the host tests never run `entire enable`, `brew`, or `curl` for real.

**`src/ext/setupService.ts` (new).**
- It holds `SetupFacts` and the step running in each repository, and fires `onDidChange`.

`refresh()`:
- Reads, in parallel:
  - `authStatus` and `graphVersion`.
  - The guide file.
  - The brain, through the existing public `brain.loadStatus(repo)`, `details(root)`, and `stateOf(root)` (`brainService.ts:96,112,138`). No new BrainService API is needed.
- Runs only while the Setup view is visible.

`runStep(root, stepId)`:
- Checks `root` with `manager.repoFor` and `stepId` against the step enum.
- Builds the command line, marks the step running, waits for the runner, then refreshes.
- After the CLI or Enable step, it runs `manager.reload({manual:false})`.
- After the Login step, it runs `entire.refresh`. A manual reload is the only thing that reads trails and Entire's session list again (`repoManager.ts:426-433, 446`), so this clears `loggedOut` and the sessions login notice.
- After a Brain step, it runs `brain.refresh()`.

`entire.showSetup` is true when either of these holds:
- `viewState` is `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, or `notEnabled`.
- Setup is pinned. Setup becomes pinned the first time the Setup view is shown in a state that isn't ready, when `entire.openSetup` runs, or when a step runs. The pin is stored in `workspaceState` and cleared only by Hide Setup.

Without the pin, a successful Enable would switch the state to `ready` and hide the page before Graph, Brain, and Connect were done.

**`src/ext/views/setupView.ts` (new).**
- A `WebviewViewProvider` modeled on `BrainView` (`views/brainView.ts`).
- Options: `enableScripts:false`, and `enableCommandUris` set to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- It redraws only when the HTML changes.
- It calls `setup.refresh()` on the first resolve and each time it becomes visible.

**`src/ext/repoManager.ts`.** Store `cliPath` and `cliSource` from `located` (`:386`) before the version check, and clear them when nothing is located.

**`src/ext/commands.ts`:**
- `entire.openSetup`: await `setContext('entire.showSetup', true)`, then run `entire.setup.focus`, and tolerate a rejection.
- New commands:
  - `entire.runSetupStep(root, stepId)`
  - `entire.checkSetup`
  - `entire.hideSetup`
- `entire.installCli` opens the install Quick Pick.
- The copy commands stay registered and stay hidden.

**`src/core/brainPage.ts`.** The `pluginMissing` and `noBrain` notices get a primary Run in Terminal button that calls `entire.runSetupStep`, and keep Copy Command as a secondary button. Add `entire.runSetupStep` to `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`.

**`src/extension.ts`:**
- Wire up the setup service, the runner, the setup view, and the search picker.
- Register the `entire.setup` view.
- Extend `EntireTestApi` with:
  - `setup`: facts, `showSetup`, the last page HTML, and a replaceable `runner`.
  - `search(query, scope)`, which returns the items.
  - `acceptSearch(item)`.

### Setup Manifest

- **The `entire.setup` webview view.** Named "Setup", first in the `entire` container, with `when: entire.showSetup`.
- **`viewsWelcome`.** For `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, and `notEnabled` on Checkpoints and Sessions: one sentence plus `[Set Up Entire](command:entire.openSetup)` and Retry.
- **`entire.openSetup`.** "Set Up Entire", in the palette with no `when`, and in the Checkpoints title overflow menu.
- **Hidden commands.** `runSetupStep`, `checkSetup`, and `hideSetup` stay out of the palette.

## Docs

**README.md:**
- Add Search and Setup sections.
- Change Getting Started to: open the Entire view and follow Setup.
- In the What the Extension Runs table:
  - Add `entire search --json` (when you search, `entire://` origins only).
  - Add `entire auth status --json` and `entire graph version --json` (while the Setup page is on screen).
  - Add a paragraph saying setup commands run only in a terminal when you click a step.
- Rewrite the read-only paragraph and the Limits bullet at line 110.
- Add `entire.search.hosted`.

**CONTRIBUTING.md:**
- Invariants: nothing reads the network or runs a brain or plugin command until the Brain, Trails, Sessions, or Setup view is on screen, or you search.
- Setup commands go only through `SetupRunner`.
- The Setup page has no script and its command links are allowlisted.

**CHANGELOG.md.** Add an entry. Leave the version as is.

Write all prose in the house style (the entire-elements-of-style skill).

## Tests

### Unit (vitest)

- `test/unit/search.test.ts`:
  - `readSearchPage` on the captured real hits: a commit with a trailer, and a session with `matchedCheckpointId`.
  - `pr` and `repo` hits are skipped, and malformed output gives `undefined`.
  - `matchesLocal` and `trailMatches`.
- `test/unit/entireCli.test.ts`:
  - `search` puts `--` before the query, and a bad query runs nothing.
  - "not logged in" gives `notLoggedIn`.

- `test/unit/setup.test.ts`:
  - `setupSteps` across fact combinations: CLI missing blocks the rest, Connect is hidden without `entireRepo`, and Connect is blocked without a login.
  - The pinned behavior.
  - `setupCommandLine` quoting for POSIX, PowerShell, and cmd, including paths with spaces or quotes.
- `test/webview/setupPage.test.ts`: escaping, and that the page links only to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- `test/webview/brainPage.test.ts`: update the button assertions at `:93` and `:101`. The check at `:148` that every allowlisted command is used must still pass.

### Extension Host

- **Scenarios in `.vscode-test.mjs`:**
  - Add `search`, `auth status --json`, and `graph version --json` replies to the healthy scenario.
  - Add a new `setup` launch with its own scenario file and `FAKE_ENTIRE_LOG`, starting not enabled. Don't reuse the `not-enabled` or `cli-missing` launches. `states.test.cjs` relies on their sidebar staying closed, and opening it would also read trails.
- **`test/integration/search.test.cjs` (new):**
  - Local hits come with no CLI call.
  - Entire's hits merge and are deduplicated.

  - No `search` call runs until search is used.

  - `showSetup` (from the test API) is true, and the page lists the expected steps.
  - With a stub runner, `runSetupStep(root,'enable')` records `entire enable`.
  - After the scenario flips `status --json` to enabled and the runner resolves, `viewState` becomes `ready` and the page stays shown because it is pinned.
  - Hide Setup clears the pin.
- **`test/integration/states.test.cjs`.** Assert from memory that the setup facts are unset and its HTML is `''` while the sidebar stays closed, as the existing invariants do (`:21-33`).
- **`test/integration/brain.test.cjs`.** Update `:288-291` for the new primary button.

## Verification

1. `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, unit tests).
2. `npm run test:host`.
3. F5 in this repository, which is enabled, has an `entire://` origin, and is logged in:
   - Check the Quick Pick ordering risk first.
   - Searching "homepage" finds commit b83de22 and session d549f207, and both open in the detail panel.

  - Windows: `irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex`.
- Keep `INSTALL_URL` at docs.entire.io (`commands.ts:16`), which redirects.

## Part 1: Search

### Core: `src/core/search.ts` (New, No `vscode` Import)

**Hit types.** A `SearchHit` union:
- `{kind:'commit', sha, subject, checkpointIds, branch?, author?, createdAt?}`. The checkpoint IDs come from `parseCheckpointIds` in `src/core/trailers.ts:26`.
- `{kind:'session', sessionId, checkpointId?, name, prompt?, agent?, branch?, createdAt?, snippet?}`.
- `{kind:'checkpoint', checkpointId, …}`.

**Reader.** `readSearchPage(value)` is a hand-written reader in the style of `schemas.ts`:
- It skips `pr` hits, `repo` hits, and malformed hits.
- It checks IDs with `isCheckpointId` and the session ID pattern. Move `SESSION_ID` out of `entireCli.ts:51`, where it isn't exported, into a shared module.

**Matching.**
- `isSearchQuery(text)` accepts 1 to 500 characters with no control characters.
- `matchesLocal(query, fields)`: every word must appear in some field, case-insensitive. Words of the form `x:y` are left out, except `branch:x`, which filters on the branch.
- `trailMatches(query, trail)` matches `#123` or `123` against the trail number, and words against the title, body, phase, and branch names.

### CLI: `src/core/entireCli.ts`

`search(cwd, query, limit, signal)` runs `['search','--json','--limit',N,'--',query]`.
- Timeout: 30 seconds.
- Failure wording: `remote: true`, so the call maps failures to `notLoggedIn` and `noAccess`.
- It rejects a query that fails `isSearchQuery` before running anything.

### Quick Pick: `src/ext/searchPicker.ts` (New)

`entire.search(scope?)`, where `scope` is `'checkpoints'|'sessions'|'trails'`, uses `createQuickPick`, following `pickTrailFilter` (`commands.ts:96`).

**Local results** draw at once, from data that is already loaded and without running any CLI command:
- Checkpoints:
  - Commits in `repo.index`: subject, SHA, checkpoint IDs.
  - The CLI's checkpoint rows. These cover checkpoints on other branches; verify the accessor in `checkpointIndex.ts` (`allRows()` or `unlinkedRows()`).
- Sessions:
  - Every entry of `manager.sessions(repo)`, which returns `{active, recent}`.
  - Fields matched: `name`, `title`, `opening`, `lastPrompt`, ID, `agent`, and `branch`.
  - Names and last prompts may be unset until the Sessions view has been shown. Never call `loadSessionRows` from search, because it prunes session state.
- Trails: `repo.trails`, when already read.

**Entire's search** adds hits after that:
- It runs only for repositories with `repo.entireRepo`, which keeps the README's promise that only `entire://` origins reach the network, and only while `entire.search.hosted` is on.
- It runs for the checkpoint and session scopes.
- It is debounced 300 ms, shows `busy`, and aborts the previous query with an `AbortController`.
- It needs at least 2 characters.

**Trails** are read once per picker:
- It runs for each repository in `manager.trailRepos` (`repoManager.ts:532`, which already applies the trails setting and view state).
- Read page 1 with `manager.cli.listTrails(root, {project: trailProject(r), repo: trailRepo(r)}, 'all', PAGE_SIZE)` and add it to a fresh `TrailPages` with `addTrailPage`.
- Then call `readTrailPages(list, fetch, () => false, {maxPages: 3})` (`trails.ts:126`) and match with `trailMatches`.

**Merging.**
- Deduplicate by checkpoint ID, session ID, and SHA.
- Every item has `alwaysShow: true`.
- Each item names its kind in its codicon (`$(git-commit)`, `$(comment-discussion)`, `$(milestone)`) and in its description.
- **Risk to check first in F5:** the stable 1.95 API has no `sortByLabel`, so VS Code may re-sort items by how well their labels match, and hide separators while you type. If that scrambles Entire's ranking, the fallback is a two-step flow: an input box for the query, then a results Quick Pick with an empty value.

**Items.**
- **Label:** the title.
- **Description:** branch, agent, and relative time.
  - `relativeTime` takes milliseconds, but `CommitRecord.authorTime` is in seconds, so multiply it by 1,000.
- **Detail:** the snippet on one line, at most 120 characters.
- **Buttons:**
  - Open in New Tab.
  - Open on entire.com, when the repository has an `entireRepo`.

**Hint items:**
- `notLoggedIn`: "Log in to Entire to search sessions on Entire". This runs the Setup Login step.
- `noAccess`: "Entire does not know this repository".
- Any other failure: "Search on Entire failed", which opens Show Log.

**Accepting an item:**
- **Commit or checkpoint with a checkpoint ID:** `panels.open({repoRoot, mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId, commitSha}, {newTab})`. The panel loads through `manager.detail`, which fetches from the checkpoint remote when needed.
- **Commit with no checkpoint:** if `git.commit(root, sha)` finds it in the clone, use `actions.showCommitDiff`. Otherwise open it on the web. `showCommitDiff` on a commit that isn't in the clone would wrongly say it changed no files (`actions.ts:80`).
- **Session the merged list knows:** `{mode:'session', sessionId}`.
- **Session the list doesn't know:** `{mode:'checkpoint', checkpointId: matchedCheckpointId, sessionId}`, which preselects the slot (`panelController.ts:434`). Session mode would say "no record" (`:422`). With no checkpoint ID, open it on the web.
- **Trail:** `panels.openTrail({repoRoot, mode:'trail', trail: number, id})`.

**Empty query.** List the newest local sessions and checkpoint commits.

**Multi-root.** Show the repository name in the description.

### Search Manifest

- **`entire.search`.** Command "Search", icon `$(search)`, with **no** palette `when`. The extension activates on its commands, and a `when` on its own context keys would hide Search until the sidebar has been opened once. When nothing is ready, the handler offers Set Up Entire.
- **Wrapper commands.** `entire.searchCheckpoints`, `entire.searchSessions`, and `entire.searchTrails`, each with its own `$(search)` icon and hidden from the palette. `view/title` items pass no arguments, so each view needs its own command.
- **Title-bar buttons.** On `navigation@0`:
  - Checkpoints and Sessions show theirs when `entire.viewState == 'ready'`.
  - Trails shows its button whenever the view is shown.
- **Setting.** `entire.search.hosted`, default `true`.

## Part 2: Entire Setup

### Steps

| Step | Done When | Runs in the Terminal | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLI | View state is past `cliMissing` and `cliTooOld` | A Quick Pick of this platform's install methods, each showing its exact command, plus Open Installation Docs. For a CLI that is too old, the upgrade path: Homebrew if the binary is under a Homebrew prefix, otherwise the script. | Nothing |
| Login | `entire auth status --json` reports `logged_in` | `entire login` | CLI |
| Enable | `repo.enabled` | `entire enable` (interactive) | CLI |
| Graph | The plugin answers `graph version`, and `.entire/agent-guide.md` exists and mentions `entire graph` | `entire plugin install graph`, then `entire graph setup` | CLI |
| Brain | `brainStatus` is not `pluginMissing`, and `manifest_state !== 'absent'` | `entire plugin install brain`, then `entire brain setup` | CLI |
| Brain Connect | Applies only when `repo.entireRepo` is set. Done when `hosted.state === 'connected'`. | `entire brain connect` | Login, a built brain |

- CLI and Enable are required. Login is recommended, because search, trails, session names, and Connect need it. Graph, Brain, and Connect are optional.
- CLI and Login apply to the whole machine. The other steps are listed for each repository.
- **CLI missing or too old.** `loadStatus` never runs in these states, so `repo.entireRepo` and `repo.status` are unknown. Enable, Graph, Brain, and Connect then show as blocked with the reason "Needs the Entire CLI", never as needed.

### Core

**`src/core/setup.ts` (new):**
- Types: `SetupStepId`, `SetupFacts`, and `setupSteps(facts) → SetupStepView[]`.
  - Each step's state is `done|needed|optional|blocked|running|unknown`, with a reason and its actions.
- `setupCommandLine(action, cli, shellKind)`:
  - The program is bare `entire` when the CLI was found on `PATH`. Otherwise it is the quoted located path: single quotes for POSIX shells, `& '…'` for PowerShell, `"…"` for cmd.
  - Only constant arguments follow the program.
  - The caller picks the shell kind from `vscode.env.shell`, not from the platform.
- `installOptions(platform, hasBrew, cliPath?)`.

**`src/core/pageKit.ts` (new).** Move `escapeHtml`, `commandHref`, `button`, and the base `STYLES` out of `brainPage.ts`. `brainPage.ts` re-exports `escapeHtml`.

**`src/core/setupPage.ts` (new):**
- Exports `setupPageHtml(model, nonce)` and `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- The page has no script, uses the Brain page's CSP, and escapes all text. Its buttons are command links with `[root, stepId]` arguments.
- Each row has:
  - A status: ✓ Done, Needed, Optional, Running in terminal…, or Needs ….
  - A title.
  - One sentence on what the step gives you.
  - A button.
- The footer has Check Again and Hide Setup. When everything is done, the page says so and keeps Hide Setup.

**`src/core/schemas.ts`.** Add `readAuthStatus`, which reads `logged_in` and `user`.

**`src/core/entireCli.ts`:**
- `authStatus(cwd)`: runs `auth status --json` with a 15-second timeout and `dedupe`.
- `graphVersion(cwd)`: runs `graph version --json` with a 5-second timeout. Generalize `isPluginMissing` (`brain.ts:240`) to take the plugin name, so that `unknown command "graph` maps to `pluginMissing`.

### Extension

**`src/ext/setupTerminal.ts` (new).** A `SetupRunner` interface with one implementation, the default terminal runner.
- `run(root, label, commandLine)` resolves to `{exitCode?}`.
- It uses one terminal for each repository root, named "Entire Setup", with `cwd: root`.
- If shell integration comes up within 5 seconds (`terminal.shellIntegration` or `onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration`, both in the 1.95 typings):
  - It runs `shellIntegration.executeCommand(commandLine)`.
  - It resolves on `window.onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` for that execution.
- Otherwise:
  - It uses `sendText`.
  - It resolves at once, and the page says "Running in terminal. Click Check Again when it finishes."
  - The service also checks again when the terminal closes and when the window regains focus.
- The runner can be replaced through the test API, the way `brain.openUrl` is (`brainService.ts:59`), so the host tests never run `entire enable`, `brew`, or `curl` for real.

**`src/ext/setupService.ts` (new).**
- It holds `SetupFacts` and the step running in each repository, and fires `onDidChange`.

`refresh()`:
- Reads, in parallel:
  - `authStatus` and `graphVersion`.
  - The guide file.
  - The brain, through the existing public `brain.loadStatus(repo)`, `details(root)`, and `stateOf(root)` (`brainService.ts:96,112,138`). No new BrainService API is needed.
- Runs only while the Setup view is visible.

`runStep(root, stepId)`:
- Checks `root` with `manager.repoFor` and `stepId` against the step enum.
- Builds the command line, marks the step running, waits for the runner, then refreshes.
- After the CLI or Enable step, it runs `manager.reload({manual:false})`.
- After the Login step, it runs `entire.refresh`. A manual reload is the only thing that reads trails and Entire's session list again (`repoManager.ts:426-433, 446`), so this clears `loggedOut` and the sessions login notice.
- After a Brain step, it runs `brain.refresh()`.

`entire.showSetup` is true when either of these holds:
- `viewState` is `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, or `notEnabled`.
- Setup is pinned. Setup becomes pinned the first time the Setup view is shown in a state that isn't ready, when `entire.openSetup` runs, or when a step runs. The pin is stored in `workspaceState` and cleared only by Hide Setup.

Without the pin, a successful Enable would switch the state to `ready` and hide the page before Graph, Brain, and Connect were done.

**`src/ext/views/setupView.ts` (new).**
- A `WebviewViewProvider` modeled on `BrainView` (`views/brainView.ts`).
- Options: `enableScripts:false`, and `enableCommandUris` set to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- It redraws only when the HTML changes.
- It calls `setup.refresh()` on the first resolve and each time it becomes visible.

**`src/ext/repoManager.ts`.** Store `cliPath` and `cliSource` from `located` (`:386`) before the version check, and clear them when nothing is located.

**`src/ext/commands.ts`:**
- `entire.openSetup`: await `setContext('entire.showSetup', true)`, then run `entire.setup.focus`, and tolerate a rejection.
- New commands:
  - `entire.runSetupStep(root, stepId)`
  - `entire.checkSetup`
  - `entire.hideSetup`
- `entire.installCli` opens the install Quick Pick.
- The copy commands stay registered and stay hidden.

**`src/core/brainPage.ts`.** The `pluginMissing` and `noBrain` notices get a primary Run in Terminal button that calls `entire.runSetupStep`, and keep Copy Command as a secondary button. Add `entire.runSetupStep` to `BRAIN_PAGE_COMMANDS`.

**`src/extension.ts`:**
- Wire up the setup service, the runner, the setup view, and the search picker.
- Register the `entire.setup` view.
- Extend `EntireTestApi` with:
  - `setup`: facts, `showSetup`, the last page HTML, and a replaceable `runner`.
  - `search(query, scope)`, which returns the items.
  - `acceptSearch(item)`.

### Setup Manifest

- **The `entire.setup` webview view.** Named "Setup", first in the `entire` container, with `when: entire.showSetup`.
- **`viewsWelcome`.** For `cliMissing`, `cliTooOld`, and `notEnabled` on Checkpoints and Sessions: one sentence plus `[Set Up Entire](command:entire.openSetup)` and Retry.
- **`entire.openSetup`.** "Set Up Entire", in the palette with no `when`, and in the Checkpoints title overflow menu.
- **Hidden commands.** `runSetupStep`, `checkSetup`, and `hideSetup` stay out of the palette.

## Docs

**README.md:**
- Add Search and Setup sections.
- Change Getting Started to: open the Entire view and follow Setup.
- In the What the Extension Runs table:
  - Add `entire search --json` (when you search, `entire://` origins only).
  - Add `entire auth status --json` and `entire graph version --json` (while the Setup page is on screen).
  - Add a paragraph saying setup commands run only in a terminal when you click a step.
- Rewrite the read-only paragraph and the Limits bullet at line 110.
- Add `entire.search.hosted`.

**CONTRIBUTING.md:**
- Invariants: nothing reads the network or runs a brain or plugin command until the Brain, Trails, Sessions, or Setup view is on screen, or you search.
- Setup commands go only through `SetupRunner`.
- The Setup page has no script and its command links are allowlisted.

**CHANGELOG.md.** Add an entry. Leave the version as is.

Write all prose in the house style (the entire-elements-of-style skill).

## Tests

### Unit (vitest)

- `test/unit/search.test.ts`:
  - `readSearchPage` on the captured real hits: a commit with a trailer, and a session with `matchedCheckpointId`.
  - `pr` and `repo` hits are skipped, and malformed output gives `undefined`.
  - `matchesLocal` and `trailMatches`.
- `test/unit/entireCli.test.ts`:
  - `search` puts `--` before the query, and a bad query runs nothing.
  - "not logged in" gives `notLoggedIn`.
  - `authStatus` parses.
  - `graphVersion` with no plugin gives `pluginMissing`.
- `test/unit/setup.test.ts`:
  - `setupSteps` across fact combinations: CLI missing blocks the rest, Connect is hidden without `entireRepo`, and Connect is blocked without a login.
  - The pinned behavior.
  - `setupCommandLine` quoting for POSIX, PowerShell, and cmd, including paths with spaces or quotes.
- `test/webview/setupPage.test.ts`: escaping, and that the page links only to `SETUP_PAGE_COMMANDS`.
- `test/webview/brainPage.test.ts`: update the button assertions at `:93` and `:101`. The check at `:148` that every allowlisted command is used must still pass.

### Extension Host

- **Scenarios in `.vscode-test.mjs`:**
  - Add `search`, `auth status --json`, and `graph version --json` replies to the healthy scenario.
  - Add a new `setup` launch with its own scenario file and `FAKE_ENTIRE_LOG`, starting not enabled. Don't reuse the `not-enabled` or `cli-missing` launches. `states.test.cjs` relies on their sidebar staying closed, and opening it would also read trails.
- **`test/integration/search.test.cjs` (new):**
  - Local hits come with no CLI call.
  - Entire's hits merge and are deduplicated.
  - A session hit opens on `matchedCheckpointId`.
  - `notLoggedIn` gives the login hint.
  - No `search` call runs until search is used.
- **`test/integration/setup.test.cjs` (new):**
  - `showSetup` (from the test API) is true, and the page lists the expected steps.
  - With a stub runner, `runSetupStep(root,'enable')` records `entire enable`.
  - After the scenario flips `status --json` to enabled and the runner resolves, `viewState` becomes `ready` and the page stays shown because it is pinned.
  - Hide Setup clears the pin.
- **`test/integration/states.test.cjs`.** Assert from memory that the setup facts are unset and its HTML is `''` while the sidebar stays closed, as the existing invariants do (`:21-33`).
- **`test/integration/brain.test.cjs`.** Update `:288-291` for the new primary button.

## Verification

1. `npm run check` (lint, typecheck, unit tests).
2. `npm run test:host`.
3. F5 in this repository, which is enabled, has an `entire://` origin, and is logged in:
   - Check the Quick Pick ordering risk first.
   - Searching "homepage" finds commit b83de22 and session d549f207, and both open in the detail panel.
   - Trails scope finds `#2923`.
4. F5 in a scratch git repository with Entire not enabled:
   - The Setup page shows.
   - Enable runs in the terminal, the views turn ready without a manual refresh, and the page stays for Graph and Brain.
   - Connect appears only for an `entire://` origin.
5. Point `entire.cliPath` at a missing file. The CLI step shows, the install Quick Pick lists this platform's commands, and Set Path still works.
6. Run `npm run smoke -- .`.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/abhi/.claude/skills/entire-elements-of-style

# The Entire Elements of Style

Apply these rules to any text you write or edit. Before returning a draft, run the checklist in section 5 against it. When a rule conflicts with your default habits (em dashes, bulleted summaries, closing recaps), the rule wins.

Source: `entirehq/Entire-Marketing`, `playbooks/entire-elements-of-style.md` at commit `f1f13092ffddc360def4a715ee816a5b52257ab5`.

---

*This is a style guide that every Entiron should use to guide their writing. Any diversions from the below rules will be treated as serious grammatical infractions.*

As you’ll see, this document is formatted using our style guide and can be used as a reference for written content. I also recommend feeding these rules to your agent of choice, so that your pre-settings are aligned with our brand preferences.

## 1. Titles and Headings Use Title Case

At Entire, we follow the [Chicago Manual of Style](https://www.chicagomanualofstyle.org/home.html) in our published content. This means that titles and headings should be written in title case, with each word besides articles, conjunctions, and prepositions capitalized.

Always run your titles and top-level headings through the [Title Case checker to be safe](https://capitalizemytitle.com/).

### 1.1 Subheadings Also Use Title Case

Any further subheadings beyond this level (which we ought to avoid for clarity’s sake) may be written in sentence case.

## 2. Grammatical Rules and Preferences

Our style acts as our first impression to the world. It dictates how we will be perceived and evaluated by developers. Therefore, we strive for clarity, consistency, and concision through the grammatical rules detailed below.

### 2.1 Active Voice

We write in active voice. In practice, this means that each sentence contains a subject and a verb, and that the subject performs the action in the sentence.

For example, these sentences are in active voice:

* *Developers write code.*
* *We shipped a new search capability.*
* *I will be at the Barcelona hackathon this weekend.*

These sentences are written in passive voice and should be avoided:

* *The code is written by developers.*
* *A new feature has been added to our CLI.*
* *The hackathon will be hosted by Entire.*

Exceptions apply in very limited cases; for example, press releases.

### 2.2 The Oxford Comma

We use the Oxford comma in lists of three or more items, consistent with the Chicago Manual of Style preferences.

For example, if we wanted to write a sentence about Marvin’s plans for the day, we would style it: *Marvin planned to mope, moan, and pout.*

If we styled the sentence: *Marvin planned to mope, moan and pout,* we imply that the final two items in the list are combined into a single activity, “moan and pout.”

Note that when two parts of a sentence are combined with “and,” there is sometimes a comma and sometimes not. More [here](https://www.grammarly.com/blog/punctuation-capitalization/comma-before-and/).

### 2.3 Goodbye, Em Dash and En Dash

Though the em dash (—) and its shorter brother, the en dash (–), are punctuation options consistent with the Chicago Manual of Style, we make a conscious departure here and strike these dashes from our content.

This is both a preference of our CEO and an effort to deter accusations of “AI slop.”

The hyphen (-) is allowed when math is involved (as a minus sign), when we show code, or when it is part of a product name, e.g. git-sync.

### 2.4 Citation Style

We [hyperlink](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/294830/the-elements-of-style-illustrated-by-strunk-white-kalman/) citations in-text, another departure from Chicago Style for ease of reading.

## 3. The Case Against AI Slop

We understand that Entirons will use AI to write early drafts of their work. However, we expect them to respect their readers and themselves by striking these signs of slop from their writing.

### 3.1 Unnecessary Lists of Three (and Lists in General)

They’re annoying, silly, and meaningless. Only use lists when appropriate, including bulleted ones, which AI agents often assemble from illogical items.

* A list
* Only makes sense
* When it’s made up of parallel additions
* Unlike this one

### 3.2 Negative Parallelism

It’s not just fluff, it’s bullshit. And unless the terms being negated are actually opposites, it doesn’t make sense.

For example, a negative parallelism might read: *It’s not just redundant, it’s repetitive.*

And could be rephrased to say: *It’s redundant*.

### 3.3 Obscuring the Point

AI drafts routinely spend a paragraph approaching the thing they want to say. We cut throat-clearing opening sentences that talk around the idea.

Common examples include: *In today's rapidly evolving..., As AI continues to..., It's worth noting..., Importantly..., In many ways..., The reality is..., When it comes to…*

When background is necessary, it can come after. But we should always lead with the point.

### 3.4 Rowing the Boat

Agents write sentences that are easy to read, but hard to understand from a distance. Do you ever read a long draft from Claude and think, *Okay, I understand all the sentences in that paragraph. But did they actually mean anything new next to one another?*

This is why we should avoid what I’d like to call “rowing the boat,” or sentences that just go through the motions. Try reading your draft out loud and see if you’d actually say each sentence. Then you’ll find great examples of unnecessary fluff to cut.

Every sentence in a paragraph should be unique, and every paragraph should further the argument.

### 3.5 Forced Conclusions

AI-generated drafts often use a summary in place of a conclusion. Once you’ve made your point, no need to restate it at the end.

## 4. A Note on Substance

Though this guide is focused on style, a few final notes on substance.

### 4.1 Know Your Audience

Assume the reader is technically sophisticated. Don't explain concepts they are likely to know (Git, commits, branches, repositories, CLIs, APIs, or other common terms) unless the explanation is necessary to the point being made. Write as one practitioner talking to another.

### 4.2 Evidence Over Adjective

To that end, when possible, choose evidence over the empty promises of adjectives and hyperbole like “seamless,” “fast,” “powerful,” or “supercharged.” Specificity is important; if you can name the action, name it.

For example, developers don't *leverage our context capabilities to enhance workflows.* They *search previous agent sessions.*

### 4.3 Avoid Absolutes

We also *always* (😉) avoid absolute terms like “always,” “never,” “everything,” and “permanent,” unless categorically true.

### 4.4 You vs. We

Think critically about perspective. In our public-facing materials, “we” means Entirons, while “you” means the developer using the product. They are not interchangeable.

### 4.5 Show, Don’t Tell

When in doubt, “show, don’t tell,” is a useful paradigm. It’s cliched for a reason!

## 5. Final Instructions for Agents

Before returning a draft, prompt your agent to:

*Remove throat-clearing, unnecessary summaries, gratuitous lists, negative parallelism, em and en dashes, unsupported superlatives, repeated conclusions, and sentences that don't add information. Replace abstract marketing language with concrete descriptions. Preserve technical terminology exactly. Do not invent facts, product behavior, commands, examples, customer claims, or capabilities. Do not rewrite technically precise language merely for stylistic variety.*

The overall order of priorities for both humans and agents is as follows:

*Accuracy → substance → clarity → concision → voice → cleverness*

When two goals conflict, the one further to the left wins. Never sacrifice technical accuracy for a cleaner sentence, or substance for a clever line, though, of course, we’re all very clever. 🤓

result.output:
**Links to entire.com.** When the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme, each commit, session, and trail gets an Open on entire.com action.

**Search.** Entire: Search opens a picker that searches checkpoints, sessions, and trails as you type. The search button in the title bar of the Checkpoints, Sessions, and Trails views opens it for that view's kind only. Results from what the views have already read appear at once: commit subjects, checkpoint IDs, session names and prompts, agents, and branches. For a repository whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme, the picker also asks Entire's search service after you pause typing, and adds the checkpoints, commits, and sessions it ranks, best first, with the part of a session's transcript that matched. Trails have no search command, so the picker reads the repository's trails once, open and closed, and matches their number (`#2923` or `2923`), title, description, phase, and branches. A query can carry Entire's filters, such as `author:alice`, `date:week`, or `branch:main`. The picker applies `branch:` to what the views have read and leaves the others to Entire. Pick a result to open it in the detail panel or the trail panel. Each result has buttons that open it in a new tab or on entire.com.

**Setup view.** The first section of the sidebar while Entire needs a step before the other views can show anything: when the CLI is missing or too old, or when Entire is not enabled in the repository. Entire: Set Up Entire opens it at any time. It lists each step with what it found:

| Step | Done when | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entire CLI | The CLI is found and is 0.12.0 or later. | A command from the [installation guide](https://docs.entire.io/installation) that you pick: Homebrew or the install script on macOS, the install script on Linux, PowerShell on Windows. Set Path picks a binary instead. |
| Login | `entire auth status` says you are logged in. | `entire login` |
| Enable Entire | `entire status` says Entire is enabled. | `entire enable` |
| Graph | The Graph plugin is installed, and `.entire/agent-guide.md` tells agents to use it. | `entire plugin install graph`, then `entire graph setup` |
| Brain | The repository has a brain. | `entire plugin install brain`, then `entire brain setup` |
| Brain Connect | The brain is connected to the repository's hosted brain. Listed only when the `origin` remote uses the `entire://` scheme. | `entire brain connect` |

Each button runs its command in a terminal named Entire Setup, where you answer the command's questions: `entire enable` asks which agents to set up, `entire login` opens your browser, and `entire brain setup` asks before it spends tokens. When the command ends, the view checks the step again, and the other views pick up the change without a refresh. The view stays in the sidebar after you use it, so the steps after Enable stay in reach, until you click Hide Setup.

**Brain view.** The last section of the sidebar, shown when Entire is enabled in the repository and collapsed until you open it. It lists what the [entire-brain plugin](https://docs.entire.io/guides/brain/overview) reports about the repository's brain: whether it is built and when it was updated, the size of its code graph, its memories, conversations, and docs, whether it is up to date, whether background updates are running, and whether it is connected to a hosted brain. Anything that needs a look is marked, with the reason on hover. These details are text: only the section's buttons can be clicked.

When the plugin is not installed, or the repository has no brain, the section says so and offers Run in Terminal, which runs the step's command as the Setup view does, and Copy Command.

The View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in your browser. The page draws the code entities in the brain and the calls and imports between them. The same button is in the section's title bar, and the command palette has Entire: View Brain. While the page's server runs, the section says where and has a Stop button. Closing the window stops it too.

## Requirements

- [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io/installation) 0.12.0 or later. The extension reads checkpoints and sessions through it. The Setup view can install it.
- Git.
- A local repository with Entire enabled (`entire enable`), opened as a trusted workspace. The Setup view can enable it.
- For the Brain view, the entire-brain plugin (`entire plugin install brain`) and a brain for the repository (`entire brain setup`).
- For the Trails view, an `entire://` origin and a login saved with `entire login`. Trails are stored on Entire, not in the clone, so the view lists them whether or not Entire is enabled there.
- For session names from Entire, the same origin and login. Without them, the Sessions view names each session by its opening prompt.
- For results from Entire's search, the same origin and login. Without them, Search matches what the views have read.

The extension looks for `entire` on your `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `/usr/local/bin`, and then asks your login shell. Set `entire.cliPath` if the binary lives somewhere else.

## Getting Started

Initial release.

- Each checkpoint's place in its session, such as 12 of 249, on its row and in the detail panel, with Previous and Next to step through the session. The selected row in the sidebar moves to the checkpoint the tab steps to.
- A checkpoint whose session data was never uploaded opens on its commit and diff, with a note that says why there is no transcript.
- Open on entire.com for commits, sessions, and trails in repositories whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme.
- Trails view for those repositories, which lists the trails that touch the repository and marks the trail on the checked-out branch. - Trail panel with the trail's description, the merge gates and CI runs of each change, and a timeline whose commits open their checkpoints. The panel draws the trail's title at once and fills in the changes and the timeline as the Entire CLI returns them. A trail opened earlier in the same window shows from that read while the panel reads it again.
- Brain view, collapsed until you open it, with what the entire-brain plugin reports about the repository's brain. Its View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in the browser.

I've built Search and the Setup flow on a new branch, `search-and-setup`, and nothing is committed yet. Lint, typecheck, all 1,786 unit tests, and every extension-host suite pass on the final code.

**Search**
- **How to open it:** run Entire: Search, or use the search button on the Checkpoints, Sessions, or Trails view to search just that kind.
- **Local results:** the checkpoints, sessions, and trails the views have already read show up as you type, without running any command.
- **Results from Entire:** after a short pause, Entire's search service adds its ranked checkpoints, commits, and sessions, including the part of a session's transcript that matched. This only happens for repositories whose remote is `entire://`, which keeps the README's promise about network use. A new setting, `entire.search.hosted`, turns it off.
- **Trails:** there's no CLI command to search trails, so the extension reads every trail, open and closed, once per search. It matches number (`#2923`), title, description, phase, and branch.
- **Opening a result:** it opens in the detail or trail panel. A session only Entire knows about opens at the checkpoint that matched.
- **Not logged in:** you get a "Log in to Entire" item, which runs the login step.

**Setup**
- **Where it is:** a new Setup section at the top of the sidebar. It appears when the CLI is missing or too old, or Entire isn't enabled in the repo. Entire: Set Up Entire opens it any time.
- **Steps:** CLI install, login, enable, Graph (install plugin, then set up), Brain (install plugin, then set up), and Brain Connect. Brain Connect only appears for `entire://` repos.
- **How each step runs:** its button runs the command in a terminal named "Entire Setup", where you answer its prompts. When the command finishes, the page checks the step again, and the other views update without a refresh.
- **Staying visible:** the section stays until you click Hide Setup, so it doesn't disappear right after Enable succeeds.
- **Brain view:** where it used to only offer Copy Command, it now also has Run in Terminal.

**Verification**
- The new host tests walk every setup step against the fake CLI, using a stand-in for the terminal so nothing gets installed or enabled. They also check that nothing new runs while the sidebar is closed.
- I ran the three new CLI calls against your real CLI in this repo. Searching "homepage" found commit b83de22 and session d549f207. Your login and Graph v0.6.0 were both detected.
- I didn't run `npm run smoke`, because it calls `entire session list`, which deletes idle session state in your real repo. It doesn't exercise the new code anyway.

**Things to know**
- **Ordering while typing:** VS Code's picker moves results whose title contains your query to the top and hides the section headings, and the extension can't turn that off. Each result says what it is (Checkpoint, Session, Trail) so it still reads clearly. I haven't looked at this by hand in a running window yet.
- **Graph step:** it counts as done when `.entire/agent-guide.md` mentions `entire graph`. It doesn't check the references in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
- **Shells without shell integration:** the terminal can't report when a command ends. The step shows "running" until you come back to the window, close the terminal, or click Check Again.
- **Docs:** I changed the README's "read-only, never runs `entire enable`" wording to match the new behavior. I also updated CONTRIBUTING and added an Unreleased entry to the changelog, without bumping the version.

231	
232	Keep it short. The driver is the meat; `SKILL.md` is the manual.
233	Structure that works:

238	> ---

240	> <App> is an Electron desktop app. For agent/automated use, drive it
241	> via the Playwright REPL at `.claude/skills/run-desktop/driver.mjs`
242	> under xvfb. Launch is slow (~10s) and the interesting UI lives in a
243	> BrowserView, not the main window - the driver handles both.

283	> ### Commands
284	>
285	> | command | what it does |
286	> |---|---|
287	> | `launch` | launch the app, wait for windows |
288	> | `ss [name]` | screenshot -> `/tmp/shots/<name>.png` |
289	> | `click <css-sel>` | click element (via DOM, not coords - see Gotchas) |
290	> | `click-text <text>` | click button/link containing text |
291	> | `type <text>` / `press <key>` | keyboard input |
292	> | `wait <css-sel>` | wait for element, 10s timeout |
293	> | `eval <js>` | evaluate in the page, print JSON |
294	> | `text [css-sel]` | print innerText |
295	> | `windows` | list all windows + webContents (find the real UI) |
296	> | `quit` | close app, exit |
