310	>
311	> ## Troubleshooting
312	>
313	> - **Launch timeout (30s):** build output missing? -> re-run the build
314	>   step. `nodeCliInspect` fuse disabled? -> Playwright can't attach;
315	>   don't disable that fuse in dev builds.
316	> - **"Missing X server":** forgot `xvfb-run`. Headless Linux needs it.
317	> - **Stale Xvfb locks:** `rm -f /tmp/.X*-lock; pkill Xvfb`
318	> - <anything else you actually hit>
319	
320	## Obstacles you will hit (and they go in Gotchas)
321	
322	These are real patterns from real Electron apps. You'll hit some subset:
323	
324	- **`firstWindow()` gives you a splash/loading screen,** not the app.
325	  Wait longer, or find the right page by URL, or wait for a specific
326	  selector that only appears when the app is actually ready.
327	
328	- **The real UI is in a BrowserView, not a BrowserWindow.** Playwright
329	  sees it as a separate "window" with a different URL. The `windows`
330	  command exists exactly for figuring this out. `getBrowserViews()`
331	  may also return empty on newer Electron - use
332	  `webContents.getAllWebContents()` instead.
333	
334	- **`locator.click()` clicks the wrong thing.** Playwright computes
335	  click coordinates relative to the main window. If your content is in
336	  a BrowserView overlay, those coordinates hit the window behind it.
337	  The driver skeleton uses `page.evaluate(el => el.click())` for this
338	  reason - DOM click bypasses coordinates entirely.
339	
340	- **Feature gates block the thing you need to test.** The app checks a
341	  plan tier, or an env flag, or a feature flag baked into SSR HTML.
342	  Find where the check happens (grep the built output for the gate
343	  name) and patch it for your local run - a `sed` on the build output,
344	  an env var override, or (for SSR-embedded flags) intercept the
345	  response via CDP `Fetch.enable` and rewrite it in-flight. Document
346	  exactly what you patched and why.
347	
348	- **contentEditable inputs** (ProseMirror, Tiptap, Slate) aren't
349	  `<textarea>`. `fill()` won't work. Focus the element, then use
350	  `keyboard.type()`. Add a `focus <sel>` command if the app has these.
351	
352	- **Electron steals stdin.** The `fs.openSync('/dev/stdin', 'r')` +
353	  `createReadStream` trick in the skeleton protects your REPL's input.
354	
355	- **Native modules fail to load** (keychain, notifications, etc.).
356	  Usually non-fatal - the core app runs, those features no-op. Note it
357	  and move on.

content.text:
The extension is running in an Extension Development Host window on your screen. That window is still open on a scratch clone of this repo if you want to click around. I sent four screenshots.

**Setup** (a new repo, Entire not enabled)
- The Setup section opens at the top of the Entire sidebar on its own.
- The CLI and Login steps show Done, with "Entire CLI 0.13.4" and your account. Enable Entire shows Needed, Graph and Brain show Optional with a Set Up button, and Brain Connect is waiting until a brain exists.
- Clicking Check Again re-read every step and the page redrew.
- I didn't click Enable or either Set Up button, since those run real setup commands. Tell me if you want me to run one in the scratch repo.

**Search** (the clone of this repo)
- The search button sits first in the Checkpoints and Trails title bars.
- Before you type anything, Entire: Search lists recent checkpoints, sessions, and trails under headings.
- Typing "homepage" added Entire's results: session d549f207 with the matching part of its transcript, and checkpoint b83de22. Trail #2923 matched as well.
- Choosing the session opened it in the detail panel at checkpoint 01M7PM7H9GQMRY1QPYW787WX0D.
- Searching "vsix" from the Trails button found #2910 by its title and #2923.

**Problems I saw**
- **Squeezed Setup view:** in a repo where Entire isn't enabled, the Checkpoints and Sessions views each repeat the "Set Up Entire" message, and the Setup checklist gets only a few lines until you collapse them. Giving the Setup view a larger starting height in `package.json` would likely fix it.
- **Ordering while typing:** as expected, VS Code moves results whose title matches the query to the top and drops the headings. Trail #2923 landed above Entire's top-ranked checkpoint. Each result still says whether it's a checkpoint, session, or trail.
- **Shared brain:** when I first gave the scratch repo this repo's `entire://` origin, Brain and Brain Connect showed Done. The CLI ties a brain to the origin, so it reported this repo's brain. The extension displayed that correctly; I switched the scratch repo to an unused origin to show the unfinished steps.

Nothing changed in your real repo. Both demo repos are scratch copies, so the Sessions view's `entire session list` only touched the clone's session state. Your branch is still uncommitted.

Driving the window took installing `playwright-core` and writing a small driver, both in the scratchpad. If you want that saved as a reusable project skill, run `/run-skill-generator`.

Merge one change of a project trail into its repository's base branch.

<trail> is a project trail number, ID, or <repo>/<number>. Without one, merges
the current branch's change. A project trail with one open change merges it, in
any repository; with several, they are listed with their review state so you
can pass one as <repo>/<number> or select it with --branch and --repo. Each
change merges on its own; merging one never merges the trail's other changes.

The trail's gates (approvals, CI checks, the base branch's CI, being up to date,
and any other configured gates) are checked first. When a blocking gate fails
or is still pending, the blocking gates are listed and nothing is merged. A
trail that conflicts with its base is never merged; resolve the conflicts first.

Pass --force to merge anyway. This bypasses the blocking gates and is recorded
on the trail; the repo's bypass policy decides who may do it. You are asked to
confirm the bypass unless --yes is passed; without a terminal to prompt on (or
with --json), --force requires --yes.

Pass --dry-run to only report whether the trail can be merged; it exits
non-zero when the merge would be refused, so it can gate CI.

After merging a native trail, the server deletes the trail's branch when the
repo's delete-branch-on-merge setting is on; your local branch is not touched.
Pass --delete-branch or --no-delete-branch to override that setting for this
merge. Before deleting the branch, the server moves any open trails based on
it onto this trail's base. It keeps the branch when one of them cannot be
moved, or for another reason the output gives. A GitHub-backed trail's
branch is left to GitHub's own auto-delete setting, so both flags are refused
there.

Usage:
  entire trail merge [<trail>] [flags]

Flags:
      --branch string                   Select a repository branch within the trail
      --delete-branch[=true|false]      Delete the trail's branch after merging, overriding the repo setting (native trails only)
      --dry-run[=true|false]            Only check whether the trail can be merged; do not merge

# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 0.1.1

## 0.1.0

Initial release.

- Checkpoints view that lists each commit on the current branch with an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, including commits that carry several checkpoints and checkpoints that no commit on the branch carries.
- Sessions view that merges running sessions, local session state, and sessions referenced by checkpoints, each with its checkpoints under it. For a repository whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme, the view lists the sessions as entire.com does: every session on every branch, under the name Entire gave it, with the checkpoints Entire lists for it. In any other repository, each session is named by the prompt that opened it.
- Detail panel with the commit, the files touched with diffs, and a transcript whose tool calls expand to show their input and result. Each prompt in the transcript names the person who sent it.
- Each checkpoint's place in its session, such as 12 of 249, on its row and in the detail panel, with Previous and Next to step through the session. The selected row in the sidebar moves to the checkpoint the tab steps to.
- A checkpoint whose session data was never uploaded opens on its commit and diff, with a note that says why there is no transcript.
- Open on entire.com for commits, sessions, and trails in repositories whose `origin` uses the `entire://` scheme.
- Trails view for those repositories, which lists the trails that touch the repository and marks the trail on the checked-out branch. A filter shows only the trails in one state: all, open, closed, or an open trail's phase of planning, building, or complete. The `entire.trails.enabled` setting turns trails off.
- Trail panel with the trail's description, the merge gates and CI runs of each change, and a timeline whose commits open their checkpoints. The panel draws the trail's title at once and fills in the changes and the timeline as the Entire CLI returns them. A trail opened earlier in the same window shows from that read while the panel reads it again.
- Brain view, collapsed until you open it, with what the entire-brain plugin reports about the repository's brain. Its View Brain button starts the plugin's graph page for the repository and opens it in the browser.
- Open Raw Transcript for the stored transcript in the agent's own format.
- Lists that show 50 rows at a time and load the next 50 when you scroll to the end, with a Load More row to click as well. The extension reads further back in the commit history only when a page needs it.
